title.zh: 卷二百五十二 列傳第十一 王景 王晏 郭從義 李洪信 武行德 楊承信 侯章
title.en: Volume 252 Biographies 11: Wang Jing, Wang Yan, Guo Congyi, Li Hongxin, Wu Xingde, Yang Chengxin, Hou Zhang
title.raw: 卷二百五十二 列傳第十一 王景 王晏 郭從義 李洪信 武行德 楊承信 侯章 Volume 252 Biographies 11: Wang Jing, Wang Yan, Guo Congyi, Li Hongxin, Wu Xingde, Yang Chengxin, Hou Zhang

sentences.zh: 王景，萊州掖人，家世力田。

translations.literal: Wang Jing was a native of Ye in Laizhou; his family for generations tilled the fields.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jing came from Ye in Laizhou. His family had farmed the land for generations.

sentences.zh: 景少倜儻，善騎射，不事生業，結里中惡少為群盜。

translations.literal: When young, Jing was bold and unconventional, skilled at mounted archery, did not pursue a livelihood, and joined local ruffians as a band of robbers.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was daring and free-spirited, an excellent horseman and archer who shunned honest work and banded with neighborhood troublemakers as outlaws.

sentences.zh: 梁大將王檀鎮滑臺，以景隸麾下，與後唐莊宗戰河上，檀有功，景嘗左右之。

translations.literal: The Liang general Wang Tan garrisoned Huatai and placed Jing under his command; when fighting Later Tang's Emperor Zhuangzong on the Yellow River, Tan won merit and Jing often assisted at his side.
translations.idiomatic: Liang general Wang Tan held Huatai and took Jing into his service. In the river battles against Later Tang's Emperor Zhuangzong, Tan earned distinction, and Jing was often at his side.

sentences.zh: 莊宗入汴，景來降，累遷奉聖都虞候。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong entered Bian, Jing came to surrender and was repeatedly promoted to commandant of the Fengsheng Guard.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhuangzong took Bian, Jing submitted and rose through successive posts to commandant of the Fengsheng Guard.

sentences.zh: 清泰末，從張敬達圍晉陽，會契丹來援，景以所部歸晉祖。

translations.literal: At the end of the Qingtai era he followed Zhang Jingda in besieging Jinyang; when the Khitan came to relieve the city, Jing brought his command over to the Jin founding emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Qingtai reign he joined Zhang Jingda's siege of Jinyang. When Khitan forces marched to relieve the city, Jing defected with his troops to the future Jin emperor.

sentences.zh: 天福初，授相州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Tianfu era he was appointed prefect of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianfu reign he was made prefect of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 范延光據鄴叛，屬郡多為所脅從，景獨分兵拒守，晉祖嘉之，遷耀州團練使。

translations.literal: Fan Yanguang seized Ye and rebelled; many subordinate prefectures were compelled to follow him, but Jing alone divided his forces to resist and hold out. The Jin founding emperor praised this and transferred him to be military commissioner of Yaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Fan Yanguang rebelled from Ye, most neighboring districts were forced to join him, but Jing alone held his ground with divided forces. The Jin emperor commended him and appointed him military commissioner of Yaozhou.

sentences.zh: 及代，會晉祖幸鄴，留為京城巡檢使，改洺州團練使。

translations.literal: When the dynasty changed, as the Jin emperor was visiting Ye, Jing was left as metropolitan patrol commissioner and then made military commissioner of Mingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the change of dynasty, while the Jin emperor was at Ye, Jing was left in charge as metropolitan patrol commissioner, then reassigned as military commissioner of Mingzhou.

sentences.zh: 開運初，授侍衛馬軍左廂都校。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Kaiyun era he was appointed commander of the left wing of the palace guard cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Kaiyun reign he was named commander of the left wing of the palace guard cavalry.

sentences.zh: 二年，契丹南侵，少帝幸澶淵，景與高行周等大破契丹眾於戚城，遷侍衛馬軍都指揮使、領鄭州防禦使，出為晉州巡檢使、知州事，拜橫海軍節度。

translations.literal: In the second year the Khitan invaded south; the young emperor went to Chanyuan. Jing, together with Gao Xingzhou and others, greatly defeated the Khitan army at Qi City. He was promoted to commander of the palace guard cavalry, concurrently defender of Zhengzhou, then sent out as patrol commissioner and acting prefect of Jinzhou, and enfeoffed as military governor of the Henghai circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the reign the Khitan swept south and the young emperor moved to Chanyuan. Jing and Gao Xingzhou won a crushing victory over the Khitan at Qi City. He was promoted to overall commander of the palace cavalry while holding the defense of Zhengzhou, then sent out to Jinzhou as patrol commissioner and acting prefect, and finally enfeoffed as military governor of Henghai.

sentences.zh: 契丹至汴，以其黨代景。

translations.literal: When the Khitan reached Bian, they replaced Jing with their own partisans.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan took Bian, they installed their own men in Jing's place.

sentences.zh: 景歸次常山，聞契丹主殂欒城，即間道歸鎮，斬關而入，契丹遁去。

translations.literal: Jing halted at Changshan; hearing that the Khitan ruler had died at Luancheng, he took a hidden route back to his command, cut through the passes to enter, and the Khitan fled.
translations.idiomatic: Jing paused at Changshan. Learning that the Khitan ruler had died at Luancheng, he slipped back to his post by a back road, forced the passes, and drove the Khitan away.

sentences.zh: 漢乾祐初，加同平章事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Han Ganyou era he was given the additional title of co-equal chief councilor.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Han Ganyou reign he was made co-equal chief councilor.

sentences.zh: 會契丹饑，幽州民多度關求食，至滄州境者五千餘人，景善懷撫，詔給田處之。

translations.literal: As the Khitan territory suffered famine, many people from Youzhou crossed the passes seeking food; more than five thousand reached the borders of Cangzhou. Jing treated them kindly and comforted them, and an edict granted them fields to settle on.
translations.idiomatic: Famine struck Khitan lands, and thousands from Youzhou crossed the border for food—over five thousand reached Cangzhou. Jing received them with care, and the court granted them land to settle.

sentences.zh: 周祖微時與景善，及即位，加兼侍中。

translations.literal: When the Zhou founder was still obscure he was on good terms with Jing; when he acceded, [Jing] was given the additional title of concurrent Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou founder had been on good terms with Jing in humbler days. When he acceded, Jing was made concurrent Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 景起身行伍，素無智略，然臨政不尚刻削，民有訟必面詰之，不至大過即諭而釋去，不為胥吏所搖，由是部民便之。

translations.literal: Jing rose from the ranks and by nature lacked strategic ability, yet in governing he did not favor harsh exactions. When the people had lawsuits he always questioned them face to face; if the offense was not grave he admonished and released them, and was not swayed by clerks and runners—therefore the people of his command found him convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Jing rose from the ranks and lacked strategic brilliance, yet he governed without harsh exactions. He questioned litigants in person and released those whose offenses were not grave, refusing to be swayed by clerks—so the people of his command found him easy to live under.

sentences.zh: 廣順初入朝，民周環等數百人，遮道留之不獲，有截景馬鐙者，俄以景為護國軍節度，歲餘，遷鎮鳳翔。

translations.literal: When he first entered court in Guangshun, several hundred people including Zhou Huan blocked the road to detain him but could not; some even seized Jing's stirrups. Soon Jing was made military governor of the Huguo army, and after more than a year he was transferred to garrison Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: When he first came to court in Guangshun, several hundred people including Zhou Huan blocked the road to keep him from leaving; some seized his stirrups. Soon he was made military governor of Huguo, and a year later transferred to Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 顯德初，封褒國公，加開府階。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiande he was enfeoffed as Duke of Bao and given Ministerial rank.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xiande he was enfeoffed as Duke of Bao and given Ministerial rank.

sentences.zh: 世宗即位，加兼中書令。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong acceded, [Jing] was given the additional title of concurrent Chief Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong acceded, Jing was made concurrent Chief Secretary.

sentences.zh: 先是，秦、鳳陷蜀，州旁蕃漢戶詣闕請收復，世宗命景與向拱率兵出大散關進討，連陷砦柵，遂命景為西面行營都部署，大破蜀軍於上邽，斬首數萬級。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Qin and Feng had fallen to Shu, neighboring Tangut and Han households went to court requesting recovery. Emperor Shizong ordered Jing and Xiang Gong to lead troops out through Dasanguan in advance against the enemy, successively capturing stockades and palisades. He then appointed Jing overall commander of the western field headquarters and inflicted a great defeat on Shu forces at Shanggui, beheading tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Qin and Feng had fallen to Shu, neighboring Tangut and Han households petitioned for their recovery. Emperor Shizong ordered Jing and Xiang Gong to march through Dasanguan, capturing stockade after stockade. He then made Jing overall commander of the western field army and routed the Shu forces at Shanggui, taking tens of thousands of heads.

sentences.zh: 是秋，秦州降。

translations.literal: That autumn Qinzhou surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn Qinzhou surrendered.

sentences.zh: 逾年，徙景鎮秦州兼西面緣邊都部署。

translations.literal: After more than a year Jing was transferred to garrison Qinzhou, concurrently overall frontier commander of the western border.
translations.idiomatic: A year later Jing was transferred to Qinzhou as overall commander of the western frontier.

sentences.zh: 恭帝即位，進封涼國公。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gongdi acceded, [Jing] was advanced and enfeoffed as Duke of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gongdi acceded, Jing was advanced to Duke of Liang.

sentences.zh: 宋初，加守太保，封太原郡王。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song he was given the additional title of Guardian Grand Mentor and enfeoffed as Prince of Taiyuan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Song he was made Guardian Grand Mentor and enfeoffed as Prince of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 建隆二年春來朝，太祖宴賜加等，復以為鳳翔節度、西面緣邊都部署。

translations.literal: In the spring of the second year of Jianlong he came to court; Taizu feasted and rewarded him with added honors, and again appointed him military governor of Fengxiang and overall frontier commander of the western border.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of the second Jianlong year he came to court. Taizu entertained him with exceptional honors and restored him as military governor of Fengxiang and overall commander of the western frontier.

sentences.zh: 四年，卒，年七十五。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he died, aged seventy-five.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourth year, at the age of seventy-five.

sentences.zh: 贈太傅，追封岐王，謚元靖。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Grand Tutor, posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Qi, with the posthumous title Yuanjing.
translations.idiomatic: The court posthumously made him Grand Tutor and Prince of Qi, with the posthumous name Yuanjing.

sentences.zh: 初，景之奔晉也，妻坐戮，二子逃獲免。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Jing had fled to Jin, his wife was executed by sitting punishment; two sons escaped and were spared.
translations.idiomatic: When Jing first defected to Jin, his wife was executed and two sons fled and survived.

sentences.zh: 晉祖待之厚，賞賜萬計，嘗問景所欲，對曰：「臣自歸國，受恩隆厚，誠無所欲。」

translations.literal: The Jin founding emperor treated him generously, with rewards numbering in the tens of thousands. He once asked Jing what he desired. Jing replied: "Since I returned to the state, I have received profound favor and truly desire nothing."
translations.idiomatic: The Jin emperor treated him lavishly, with gifts beyond counting. Once he asked what Jing wanted. Jing answered, "Since I came over, Your Majesty's kindness has been boundless. I truly want for nothing."

sentences.zh: 固問之，景稽顙再拜曰：「臣昔為卒，嘗負胡床從隊長出入，屢過官妓侯小師家，意甚慕之。

translations.literal: Pressed further, Jing bowed his forehead to the ground and said twice: "When I was formerly a soldier, I once carried a folding camp-chair following the squad leader in and out, and often passed the house of the official courtesan Hou Xiaoshi; I greatly admired her in my heart.
translations.idiomatic: Pressed again, Jing kowtowed and said, "When I was a common soldier I used to carry a camp-chair for my squad leader and often passed the house of the courtesan Hou Xiaoshi. I have long admired her.

sentences.zh: 今妻被誅，誠得小師為妻足矣。」

translations.literal: Now that my wife has been executed, if I could truly have Xiaoshi as my wife, that would be enough."
translations.idiomatic: My wife is gone. If I could have Xiaoshi for my wife, that is all I ask."

sentences.zh: 晉祖大笑，即以小師賜景。

translations.literal: The Jin founding emperor laughed greatly and immediately bestowed Xiaoshi on Jing.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin emperor laughed and at once gave him Xiaoshi.

sentences.zh: 景甚寵嬖之，後累封楚國夫人。

translations.literal: Jing greatly favored and doted on her; later she was repeatedly ennobled as Lady of the state of Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Jing cherished her devotedly, and she was later raised to Lady of Chu.

sentences.zh: 侯氏嘗盜景金數百兩，私遺舊人，景知而不責。

translations.literal: Lady Hou once stole several hundred taels of Jing's gold and secretly gave them to old acquaintances; Jing knew but did not punish her.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Hou once stole several hundred taels of his gold to give old friends in secret. Jing knew and said nothing.

sentences.zh: 性謙退，折節下士，每朝廷使至，雖卑位必降階送迎，周旋盡禮。

translations.literal: By nature he was modest and retiring, restraining himself to honor scholars; whenever an envoy from court arrived, though of humble rank he would descend the steps to welcome and send off, observing full courtesy in every turn.
translations.idiomatic: He was modest by nature and humbled himself before men of learning. Whenever a court envoy arrived, however lowly the man's rank, Jing would come down the steps to greet and see him off with full ceremony.

sentences.zh: 左右或曰：「王位尊崇，無自謙抑。」

translations.literal: Those at his side sometimes said: "Your princely rank is exalted; there is no need to humble yourself."
translations.idiomatic: His attendants would say, "Your Highness's station is lofty—there is no need for such self-abasement."

sentences.zh: 景曰：「人臣重君命，固當如是，我惟恐不謹耳。」

translations.literal: Jing said: "As subjects we honor the ruler's command; it is right to act thus. I only fear I am not careful enough."
translations.idiomatic: Jing replied, "A subject honors the sovereign's commission—that is how it should be. I only fear I am not courteous enough."

sentences.zh: 初封郡王，朝廷以吏部尚書張昭將命，景尤加禮重，以萬餘緡遺昭。

translations.literal: When he was first enfeoffed as commandery prince, the court sent Minister of Personnel Zhang Zhao with the commission. Jing showed him especial courtesy and presented Zhao with more than ten thousand strings of cash.
translations.idiomatic: When he was first made a commandery prince, the court sent Zhang Zhao, Minister of Personnel, with the patent of enfeoffment. Jing treated him with exceptional respect and gave him more than ten thousand strings of cash.

sentences.zh: 左右或言其過厚，景曰：「我在行伍間，即聞張尚書名，今使於我，是朝廷厚我也，豈可以往例為限耶？」

translations.literal: Those at his side said the gift was excessive. Jing said: "When I was in the ranks I already heard Minister Zhang's name. That he is envoy to me now means the court honors me—how can I be bound by former precedent?"
translations.idiomatic: Attendants said the gift was too lavish. Jing said, "Even in the ranks I knew Minister Zhang's reputation. That the court sends him to me is an honor—how can I measure that by old custom?"

sentences.zh: 景子廷義、廷睿、廷訓。

translations.literal: Jing's sons were Tingyi, Tingrui, and Tingxun.
translations.idiomatic: Jing's sons were Tingyi, Tingrui, and Tingxun.

sentences.zh: 廷訓至驍衛大將軍致仕。

translations.literal: Tingxun rose to Grand General of the Valiant Guard and retired from office.
translations.idiomatic: Tingxun rose to Grand General of the Valiant Guard before retiring.

sentences.zh: 廷義起家供奉官，改如京副使，以善騎射，周世宗擢為虎捷都虞候，遷龍捷右第二軍都校、領珍州刺史。

translations.literal: Tingyi began as a palace attendant, then became deputy commissioner for the capital; for skill in mounted archery, Zhou Shizong promoted him to commandant of the Tiger Swift Guard, then transferred him to colonel of the second army of the right Dragon Swift wing, concurrently prefect of Zhenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Tingyi entered service as a palace attendant, then became deputy commissioner for the capital. His horsemanship won him promotion under Zhou Shizong to commandant of the Tiger Swift Guard, then colonel of the second right Dragon Swift army while holding Zhenzhou.

sentences.zh: 宋初，改內外馬步軍副都軍頭。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song he was made deputy commander-in-chief of the inner and outer horse and foot armies.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Song he was made deputy commander of the inner and outer horse and foot armies.

sentences.zh: 乾德四年，與韓重贇率師護治滑州靈河新堤。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Qiande, together with Han Chongyun he led troops to supervise repair of the new embankment on the Ling River at Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth Qiande year he and Han Chongyun led troops to repair the new Ling River embankment at Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 六年，增治京城，又命廷義董其役。

translations.literal: In the sixth year the capital was further improved; Tingyi was again ordered to direct the work.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year further work was done on the capital, and Tingyi was put in charge again.

sentences.zh: 開寶二年，加領橫州團練使，從征太原。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaibao he was additionally made military commissioner of Hengzhou and followed the campaign against Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the second Kaibao year he was given Hengzhou as well and joined the Taiyuan campaign.

sentences.zh: 廷義性勇敢，親鼓士乘城，獨免胄，矢中其腦而顛，經宿卒，年四十七。

translations.literal: Tingyi was brave by nature; he personally beat the drums to urge the men onto the walls, alone removed his helmet, was struck in the head by an arrow and fell, and died after one night, aged forty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: Tingyi was fearless. He beat the drums himself to lead the assault on the walls, bareheaded, took an arrow in the head, and died the next night at forty-seven.

sentences.zh: 太祖甚惜之，優詔贈建雄軍節度。

translations.literal: Taizu deeply regretted it and by gracious edict posthumously made him military governor of Jianxiong.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu mourned him deeply and by special edict posthumously made him military governor of Jianxiong.

sentences.zh: 廷睿性驕傲，好夸誕，每言：「我當代王景之子。」

translations.literal: Tingrui was proud by nature and fond of boastful exaggeration; he often said: "I am the son who should replace Wang Jing."
translations.idiomatic: Tingrui was arrogant and fond of grand talk. He liked to say, "I am the son who should succeed Wang Jing."

sentences.zh: 聞者咸笑之，因目為『王當代』。

translations.literal: Hearers all laughed at this, and so he was nicknamed "Wang the Successor."
translations.idiomatic: Everyone who heard it laughed, and people nicknamed him "Wang the Successor."

sentences.zh: 王晏，徐州滕人，家世力田。

translations.literal: Wang Yan was a native of Teng in Xuzhou; his family for generations tilled the fields.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yan came from Teng in Xuzhou. His family had farmed for generations.

sentences.zh: 晏少壯勇無賴，嘗率群寇行攻劫。

translations.literal: When young Yan was bold, fierce, and unruly; he once led a band of robbers in raids and plunder.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Yan was fierce and lawless and led gangs in robbery and pillage.

sentences.zh: 梁末，徐方大亂，屬邑皆為他盜所剽，惟晏鄉里恃晏獲全。

translations.literal: At the end of Liang, the Xu region was greatly disturbed; subordinate districts were all plundered by other bandits, but only Yan's home village, relying on Yan, was kept intact.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Liang, chaos engulfed Xu. Neighboring districts were looted by other bandits, but Yan's home village alone was spared because of him.

sentences.zh: 後唐同光中，應募隸禁軍，累遷奉國小校。

translations.literal: In the Later Tang Tongguang era he answered the levy and joined the palace army, rising through posts to junior officer of the Fengguo Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Under Later Tang in the Tongguang era he enlisted in the palace army and rose to junior officer of the Fengguo Guard.

sentences.zh: 晉開運末，與本軍都校趙暉、忠衛都校侯章等戍陜州。

translations.literal: At the end of Jin Kaiyun, together with his army's colonel Zhao Hui, the Zhongwei Guard's colonel Hou Zhang, and others, he garrisoned Shaanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Jin Kaiyun reign he garrisoned Shaanzhou with his colonel Zhao Hui, Zhongwei colonel Hou Zhang, and others.

sentences.zh: 會契丹至汴，遣其將劉愿據陜，恣行暴虐，晏與暉等謀曰：「今契丹南侵，天下洶洶，英雄豪傑固當乘時自奮。

translations.literal: When the Khitan reached Bian, they sent their general Liu Yuan to hold Shaan and wantonly practiced cruelty and oppression. Yan and Hui and the others plotted, saying: "Now the Khitan invade south and the realm is in turmoil; heroes and great men ought surely to seize the moment and rouse themselves.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan took Bian they sent Liu Yuan to hold Shaan, where he ruled with savage cruelty. Yan and Hui plotted together: "The Khitan are south, the realm is in chaos—this is the hour for a true man to rise.

sentences.zh: 且聞太原劉公威德遠被，人心歸服，若殺愿送款河東，為天下倡首，則取富貴如反掌耳。」

translations.literal: Moreover we hear that Lord Liu of Taiyuan's prestige and virtue extend far and men's hearts submit to him. If we kill Yuan and send allegiance to Hedong, taking the lead for the realm, then gaining wealth and rank would be like turning the palm."
translations.idiomatic: We hear that Liu of Taiyuan's fame reaches far and men flock to him. Kill Yuan, open the gates to Hedong, and lead the realm—fortune and rank would be ours in a stroke."

sentences.zh: 暉等然之。

translations.literal: Hui and the others agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Hui and the rest agreed.

sentences.zh: 晏乃率敢死士數人夜踰城，入府署，劫庫兵給其徒，遲明，斬愿首級府門外。

translations.literal: Yan then led several dare-to-die men by night over the wall, entered the prefectural compound, seized weapons from the arsenal for his followers, and at dawn beheaded Yuan and displayed his head outside the prefectural gate.
translations.idiomatic: Yan led a handful of daredevils over the wall by night into the yamen, seized arms from the arsenal for his men, and at dawn cut off Yuan's head and hung it outside the gate.

sentences.zh: 眾請暉為帥，章為本城副指揮使、內外巡檢使兼都虞候；

translations.literal: The multitude asked Hui to be commander; Zhang was made deputy commander of the local garrison, inner and outer patrol commissioner, and concurrent commandant.
translations.idiomatic: The troops made Hui their commander. Zhang became deputy garrison commander, patrol commissioner inside and out, and commandant as well;

sentences.zh: 遣其子漢倫奉表晉陽。

translations.literal: they sent his son Hanlun to present a memorial at Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: and Yan sent his son Hanlun to Jinyang with a letter of submission.

sentences.zh: 時漢祖雖建號，威聲未振，得晏等來歸，甚喜，即日以暉為保平軍節度，章為鎮國軍節度，晏為絳州防禦使，仍領舊職。

translations.literal: At that time though the Han founding emperor had established his title, his prestige was not yet strong; receiving Yan and the others coming over, he was greatly pleased. That very day he made Hui military governor of Baoping, Zhang military governor of Zhenguo, and Yan defender of Jiangzhou, each retaining former duties.
translations.idiomatic: The Han emperor had taken the throne but his name still rang small. Yan's defection delighted him. That same day he made Hui governor of Baoping, Zhang of Zhenguo, and Yan defender of Jiangzhou while keeping their old posts.

sentences.zh: 既而暉等表晏始謀功為第一，遷建雄軍節度。

translations.literal: Soon Hui and the others memorialized that Yan's merit in initiating the plot was foremost, and he was transferred to military governor of Jianxiong.
translations.idiomatic: Hui and the others then reported that Yan had conceived the plot and deserved first credit. He was promoted to military governor of Jianxiong.

sentences.zh: 漢祖入汴，加同平章事。

translations.literal: When the Han founding emperor entered Bian, Yan was given the additional title of co-equal chief councilor.
translations.idiomatic: When the Han emperor entered Bian, Yan was made co-equal chief councilor.

sentences.zh: 周祖即位，加兼侍中。

translations.literal: When the Zhou founder acceded, [Yan] was given the additional title of concurrent Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhou founder acceded, Yan was made concurrent Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 廣順元年，劉崇侵晉州，晏閉關不出，設伏城上。

translations.literal: In the first year of Guangshun, Liu Chong invaded Jinzhou; Yan closed the passes and would not come out, setting ambushes atop the walls.
translations.idiomatic: In the first Guangshun year, Liu Chong invaded Jinzhou. Yan shut the gates and refused to emerge, posting ambushes on the walls.

sentences.zh: 幷人以為怯，競攀堞而登，晏麾伏兵擊之，顛死者甚眾，遂焚橋遁。

translations.literal: The Bing men thought him cowardly and scrambled up the battlements to climb; Yan waved his hidden troops to strike them, and very many fell headlong to their deaths. He then burned the bridge and fled.
translations.idiomatic: The Bing troops thought him cowardly and swarmed the battlements. Yan signaled his ambush, and many fell to their deaths. He then burned the bridge and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 遣漢倫追北數十里，斬首百餘級，擢漢倫濱州刺史。

translations.literal: He sent Hanlun in pursuit north for several tens of li, beheaded more than a hundred heads, and promoted Hanlun to prefect of Binzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Hanlun in pursuit for dozens of li, took more than a hundred heads, and promoted Hanlun to prefect of Binzhou.

sentences.zh: 八月來朝，周祖以晏家彭城，授武寧軍節度，俾榮其鄉里。

translations.literal: In the eighth month he came to court; because Yan's family was from Pengcheng, the Zhou founder appointed him military governor of the Wuning army so that his home district might be honored.
translations.idiomatic: He came to court in the eighth month. Because Yan's family came from Pengcheng, the Zhou founder made him military governor of Wuning so his homeland might share in the honor.

sentences.zh: 三年，周祖征兗州，次張康鎮，晏來朝，獻馬七匹，賜襲衣、金帶。

translations.literal: In the third year, as the Zhou founder campaigned against Yanzhou and halted at Zhangkang town, Yan came to court, presented seven horses, and was granted ceremonial robes and a gold belt.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, while the Zhou founder campaigned against Yanzhou and halted at Zhangkang, Yan came to court with seven horses and received ceremonial robes and a gold belt.

sentences.zh: 親郊畢，封滕國公，加開府階。

translations.literal: When the suburban sacrifice was completed, he was enfeoffed as Duke of Teng and given Ministerial rank.
translations.idiomatic: After the suburban sacrifice he was enfeoffed as Duke of Teng and given Ministerial rank.

sentences.zh: 世宗即位，加兼中書令。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong acceded, [Yan] was given the additional title of concurrent Chief Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong acceded, Yan was made concurrent Chief Secretary.

sentences.zh: 初，晏至鎮，悉召故時同為盜者遺以金帛，從容置酒語之曰：「吾鄉素多盜，我與諸君昔嘗為之。

translations.literal: When Yan first reached his command, he summoned all who had formerly been robbers with him, gave them gold and silk, and over wine said at ease: "Our district has always had many bandits; you and I once did this together.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan first took his post he summoned his old bandit comrades, gave them gold and silk, and over wine said gently, "Our country has always had its thieves—you and I were among them once.

sentences.zh: 後來者固當出諸君之下，為我告諭，令不復為，若不能改，吾必盡滅其族。」

translations.literal: Those who come later should surely rank below you; convey this for me and tell them not to do it again. If they cannot reform, I will exterminate their clans to the last."
translations.idiomatic: Anyone who comes after you must stay beneath you. Tell them to stop—or I will wipe out their families to the last man."

sentences.zh: 由是境內安靜，吏民詣闕舉留，請為晏立衣錦碑。

translations.literal: Thereby the territory within became peaceful and quiet; officials and people went to court to petition to retain him and asked to erect for Yan a "return in glory" stele.
translations.idiomatic: The district grew quiet. Officials and commoners petitioned the throne to keep him and asked for a "glorious return" stele in his honor.

sentences.zh: 世宗初，復請立德政碑。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shizong's reign they again asked to erect a stele of virtuous administration.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Shizong's reign they asked again for a stele praising his rule.

sentences.zh: 世宗命比部郎中、知制誥張正撰文賜之，詔改其鄉里為使相鄉勳德里，私門立戟。

translations.literal: Shizong ordered Zhang Zheng, director of the Ministry of Revenue's comparisons bureau and drafter of edicts, to compose the text and bestow it; an edict changed his home village to Xunde Lane in the Xiangxiang of chief ministers, and halberds were set up at his private gate.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong had Zhang Zheng compose the inscription, renamed his home village Xunde Lane in Ministers' Township, and ordered halberds set before his gate.

sentences.zh: 未幾，改河南尹、西京留守。

translations.literal: Before long he was made metropolitan magistrate of Henan and western capital regent.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made metropolitan magistrate of Henan and regent of the western capital.

sentences.zh: 顯德三年，移鳳翔節度。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xiande he was transferred to military governor of Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the third Xiande year he was transferred to Fengxiang as military governor.

sentences.zh: 六年，從世宗北征，為益津關一路馬軍都部署，韓令坤副焉，遂平三關。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he followed Shizong on the northern campaign as overall commander of cavalry on the Yijin Pass route, with Han Lingkun as deputy, and thereby pacified the three passes.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he joined Shizong's northern campaign as cavalry commander on the Yijin route with Han Lingkun as deputy, and helped secure the three frontier passes.

sentences.zh: 太祖即位，進封趙國公。

translations.literal: When Taizu took the throne, Yan was advanced to Duke of Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu took the throne, Yan was advanced to Duke of Zhao.

sentences.zh: 從征李筠，師還，改安遠軍節度。

translations.literal: He followed the campaign against Li Yun; when the army returned he was made military governor of Anyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the campaign against Li Yun and, on the army's return, was made military governor of Anyuan.

sentences.zh: 乾德元年，進封韓國公，上章請老，拜太子太師致仕。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qiande he was advanced to Duke of Han, submitted a memorial requesting retirement, and was made Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent with retirement from office.
translations.idiomatic: In the first Qiande year he was raised to Duke of Han, asked to retire, and was made Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent with permission to leave office.

sentences.zh: 每朝會，令綴中書門下班。

translations.literal: At each court assembly he was ordered to take place in the row after the Zhongshu Gate class.
translations.idiomatic: At court assemblies he was placed in the row just after the chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 俄歸洛陽別墅。

translations.literal: Soon he returned to his villa at Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he withdrew to his villa at Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 四年冬，卒，年七十七。

translations.literal: In the winter of the fourth year he died, aged seventy-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the winter of the fourth year, at seventy-seven.

sentences.zh: 廢朝三日，贈中書令。

translations.literal: Court was suspended for three days; he was posthumously made Chief Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Court mourned three days and posthumously made him Chief Secretary.

sentences.zh: 初，晏為軍校，與平陸人王興善，其妻亦相為娣姒。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Yan was an army officer, he was on good terms with Wang Xing of Pinglu; their wives were also sisters-in-law to each other.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan was still a junior officer he was close to Wang Xing of Pinglu, and their wives were sisters-in-law.

sentences.zh: 晏既貴，乃薄興，興不能平。

translations.literal: After Yan became eminent he treated Xing coldly; Xing could not accept this.
translations.idiomatic: Once Yan rose high he snubbed Xing, who could not bear the slight.

sentences.zh: 晏妻病，興語人曰：「吾能治之。」

translations.literal: When Yan's wife fell ill, Xing told others: "I can cure her."
translations.idiomatic: When Yan's wife fell ill, Xing told people, "I can cure her."

sentences.zh: 晏遽訪興，興曰：「我非能醫，但以公在陜時止一妻，今妓妾甚眾，得非待糟糠之薄，致夫人怏怏成疾耶？

translations.literal: Yan hurried to visit Xing. Xing said: "I am not able to practice medicine, but when you were at Shaan you had only one wife; now your singing girls and concubines are very many—could it not be that treating your wife of humble days too lightly has made the lady displeased and brought on illness?
translations.idiomatic: Yan rushed to see him. Xing said, "I am no physician—but in Shaan you had one wife and now a houseful of concubines. Have you neglected the woman who stood by you in poverty and made your lady sick with grief?

sentences.zh: 若能斥去女侍，夫人之疾可立愈。」

translations.literal: If you can drive away the female attendants, the lady's illness can be cured at once."
translations.idiomatic: Send the concubines away and your wife will recover at once."

sentences.zh: 晏以為謗己，乃誣以他事，悉案誅其夫妻。

translations.literal: Yan thought Xing was slandering him, so he fabricated other charges and had husband and wife investigated and executed together.
translations.idiomatic: Yan took this for slander, trumped up other charges, and had husband and wife executed together.

sentences.zh: 守西洛日，白重贊鎮河陽，時世宗征淮南，重贊慮幷人乘間為寇，因葺城壘，且約晏為援。

translations.literal: While holding the western capital, Bai Chongzan garrisoned Heyang. At that time Shizong was campaigning in Huainan; Chongzan feared the Bing people would seize the interval to raid, so he repaired walls and ramparts and also arranged with Yan as reinforcement.
translations.idiomatic: While Yan held the western capital, Bai Chongzan held Heyang. Shizong was campaigning in Huainan, and Chongzan feared the Bingzhou forces might strike while he was weak, so he strengthened his walls and asked Yan for support.

sentences.zh: 晏意欲兼有三城，即與漢倫同率兵赴之。

translations.literal: Yan intended to take all three cities for himself and immediately led troops with Hanlun to go to his aid.
translations.idiomatic: Yan meant to seize all three cities for himself and marched with Hanlun to Heyang.

sentences.zh: 重贊聞其來，拒不納，遣人語之曰：「公在陜州已立大功，河陽小城不煩枉駕。」

translations.literal: Chongzan heard he was coming, refused to admit him, and sent someone to say: "Your Lordship already achieved great merit at Shaanzhou; this small city of Heyang does not trouble you to come in person."
translations.idiomatic: Chongzan heard he was coming and shut the gates, sending word: "You won great glory at Shaanzhou. This little town of Heyang hardly needs your presence."

sentences.zh: 慚不能對，遂引兵還。

translations.literal: Ashamed, Yan could not reply and thereupon led his troops back.
translations.idiomatic: Yan, shamed, had no answer and marched home.

sentences.zh: 郭從義

translations.literal: Guo Congyi
translations.idiomatic: Guo Congyi

sentences.zh: 郭從義，其先沙陀部人。

translations.literal: Guo Congyi—his ancestors were people of the Shatuo tribe.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Congyi's forebears were of the Shatuo tribe.

sentences.zh: 父紹古，事後唐武皇忠謹，特見信任，賜姓李氏。

translations.literal: His father Shaogu served Later Tang's Martial Emperor with loyalty and care and was especially trusted; he was granted the surname Li.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shaogu served Later Tang's Martial Emperor with loyal care, won exceptional trust, and was granted the surname Li.

sentences.zh: 紹古卒，從義才丱角，莊宗畜於宮中，與諸子齒。

translations.literal: When Shaogu died, Congyi was only a child in topknot; Zhuangzong raised him in the palace and ranked him with his own sons.
translations.idiomatic: When Shaogu died, Congyi was still a small boy. Zhuangzong raised him in the palace alongside his own sons.

sentences.zh: 明宗與紹古同事武皇，情好款狎，即位，以從義補內職，累遷內園使。

translations.literal: Mingzong and Shaogu had served the Martial Emperor together and were close in affection; when Mingzong took the throne he appointed Congyi to an inner palace post, and he rose through posts to commissioner of the inner gardens.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong had served with Shaogu under the Martial Emperor and held the family dear. On his accession he gave Congyi a palace post, and Congyi rose to commissioner of the inner gardens.

sentences.zh: 晉天福初，始復姓郭氏。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jin Tianfu he first restored the surname Guo.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jin Tianfu reign he resumed the surname Guo.

sentences.zh: 坐事出為宿州團練副使。

translations.literal: For an offense he was sent out as deputy military commissioner of Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After an offense he was sent out as deputy military commissioner of Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 丁內艱北歸，遂家太原。

translations.literal: Upon his mother's death he returned north and then made his home at Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died he went north for mourning and settled in Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 漢祖在鎮，表為馬步軍都虞候，屢率師破破契丹於代北，及建大號，從義首贊其謀，擢鄭州防禦使，充東南道行營都虞候，領首軍自太行路渡河。

translations.literal: While the Han founding emperor was in his commandery, he memorialized to make Congyi commandant of the horse and foot armies; Congyi repeatedly led troops to defeat the Khitan north of Dai, and when the great title was established Congyi was first to support the plan. He was promoted to defender of Zhengzhou, made overall commandant of the southeast campaign headquarters, and led the vanguard army crossing the river by the Taihang route.
translations.idiomatic: While the Han emperor still held his fief, he named Congyi commandant of horse and foot. Congyi repeatedly beat the Khitan north of Dai. When the Han throne was proclaimed, Congyi was first to back the plan. He was made defender of Zhengzhou, commandant of the southeast campaign, and led the vanguard across the Taihang route.

sentences.zh: 漢祖入汴，以為河北都巡檢使。

translations.literal: When the Han founding emperor entered Bian, Congyi was made overall patrol commissioner of Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: When the Han emperor entered Bian, Congyi was made overall patrol commissioner of Hebei.

sentences.zh: 杜重威據大名叛，以為行營諸軍都虞候，重威降，為鎮寧軍節度。

translations.literal: When Du Chongwei held Daming and rebelled, Congyi was made commandant of all armies in the campaign headquarters; when Chongwei surrendered, Congyi was made military governor of Zhenning.
translations.idiomatic: When Du Chongwei rebelled from Daming, Congyi was made commandant of the campaign armies. After Chongwei surrendered, Congyi was made military governor of Zhenning.

sentences.zh: 趙思綰之叛，為行營都部署，賜戎裝、器仗、金帶。

translations.literal: When Zhao Sihuan rebelled, Congyi was made overall campaign commander and was granted military dress, weapons, and a gold belt.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao Sihuan rebelled, Congyi was made overall campaign commander and given military dress, arms, and a gold belt.

sentences.zh: 師至永興，圍其城，即以從義為永興軍節度。

translations.literal: When the army reached Yongxing and besieged its city, Congyi was immediately made military governor of the Yongxing circuit.
translations.idiomatic: The army reached Yongxing and laid siege, and Congyi was at once made military governor of Yongxing.

sentences.zh: 思綰糧盡，城中人相食，從義繫書矢上，射入城中，說思綰令降，仍表於朝廷，許以華州節制。

translations.literal: Sihuan's grain was exhausted and people in the city ate one another. Congyi tied a letter to an arrow, shot it into the city, and urged Sihuan to surrender; he also memorialized the court, promising him control of Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Sihuan's stores ran out and the besieged turned to cannibalism. Congyi shot a letter into the city urging surrender and asked the court to promise him Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 隱帝從其計，即遣使諭思綰，思綰開門納款。

translations.literal: Emperor Yindi followed this plan and immediately sent envoys to instruct Sihuan; Sihuan opened the gates and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yindi agreed and sent envoys. Sihuan opened the gates and submitted.

sentences.zh: 翌日，從義具軍容入城，憩候館中，思綰入謁，即令武士執之，並其黨三百餘人悉斬於市，以功加同平章事。

translations.literal: The next day Congyi entered the city in full military array, rested at the reception lodge; Sihuan came to pay respects, and Congyi immediately ordered warriors to seize him. Together with more than three hundred of his partisans they were all beheaded in the market. For this merit he was given the additional title of co-equal chief councilor.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Congyi entered in full array and waited at the guest lodge. When Sihuan came to pay respects, Congyi had his men seize him and more than three hundred followers and beheaded them all in the market. For this he was made co-equal chief councilor.

sentences.zh: 周廣順初，加兼侍中，移鎮許州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhou Guangshun he was given the additional title of Palace Attendant and transferred to garrison Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhou Guangshun he was made Palace Attendant as well and transferred to Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 顯德初，親郊，加檢校太師。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiande, at the imperial suburban sacrifice, he was given the additional title of Inspector Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xiande, at the suburban sacrifice, he was made Inspector Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 世宗將征劉崇，從義適來朝，因請扈從，世宗甚悅，改天平軍節度，即令從符彥卿破契丹於忻口。

translations.literal: When Shizong was about to campaign against Liu Chong, Congyi happened to come to court and thereupon asked to follow in attendance. Shizong was greatly pleased, changed him to military governor of Tianping, and immediately ordered him to follow Fu Yanqing in defeating the Khitan at Xinkou.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong prepared to campaign against Liu Chong, Congyi happened to be at court and asked to join him. Shizong was delighted, made him governor of Tianping, and sent him with Fu Yanqing to defeat the Khitan at Xinkou.

sentences.zh: 師還，以功加兼中書令。

translations.literal: When the army returned, for merit he was given the additional title of concurrent Chief Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: On the army's return he was given the concurrent title of Chief Secretary for his service.

sentences.zh: 四年，從征淮南，移鎮徐州。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he followed the Huainan campaign and was transferred to garrison Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he joined the Huainan campaign and was transferred to Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 及世宗自迎鑾至泗州，見於行在。

translations.literal: When Shizong came from welcoming the imperial carriage to Sizhou, Congyi was received at the mobile court.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong reached Sizhou after escorting the imperial carriage, Congyi was received at the field headquarters.

sentences.zh: 恭帝即位，加開府階。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gong took the throne, Congyi was given the rank of opening a government office.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gong succeeded, Congyi was granted the privilege of an independent staff.

sentences.zh: 宋初，加守中書令。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song he was given the additional title of Guardian Chief Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Song he was made Guardian Chief Secretary.

sentences.zh: 太祖征揚州，從義迎謁於路，願扈從，不允。

translations.literal: When Taizu campaigned against Yangzhou, Congyi met and paid respects on the road, asking to follow in attendance; this was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu marched on Yangzhou, Congyi met him on the road and asked to join the campaign, but Taizu refused.

sentences.zh: 乾德二年，又為河中尹、護國國節度。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qiande he again became metropolitan magistrate of Hezhong and military governor of Huguo.
translations.idiomatic: In the second Qiande year he was again made metropolitan magistrate of Hezhong and military governor of Huguo.

sentences.zh: 六年，以疾歸京師。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, because of illness he returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year illness brought him back to the capital.

sentences.zh: 開寶二年，改左金吾衛上將軍。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaibao he was changed to Grand General of the Left Golden Crow Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the second Kaibao year he was made Grand General of the Left Golden Crow Guard.

sentences.zh: 逾年，上章請老，拜太子太師致仕。

translations.literal: After more than a year he submitted a memorial requesting retirement and was made Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent with retirement from office.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he asked to retire and was made Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent with permission to leave office.

sentences.zh: 四年，卒，年六十三，贈中書令。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he died, aged sixty-three, and was posthumously made Chief Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourth year at sixty-three. The court posthumously made him Chief Secretary.

sentences.zh: 從義性重厚，有謀略，多技藝，尤善飛白書。

translations.literal: Congyi's nature was grave and substantial; he had stratagems and many skills, especially excelling at feibai calligraphy.
translations.idiomatic: Congyi was steady and thoughtful, skilled in many arts, and especially masterful at feibai calligraphy.

sentences.zh: 初，思綰之叛也，巡檢使喬守溫遁去，姬妾悉入思綰，思綰敗，從義盡取之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Sihuan rebelled, patrol commissioner Qiao Shouwen fled; his concubines all fell into Sihuan's hands. When Sihuan was defeated, Congyi took them all.
translations.idiomatic: When Sihuan rebelled, patrol commissioner Qiao Shouwen fled and left his concubines behind. Sihuan took them, and when he fell Congyi claimed them all.

sentences.zh: 守溫詣從義求其愛妾，雖不敢拒，而心銜焉，遂發守溫逃遁事，坐棄市，人皆冤之。

translations.literal: Shouwen came to Congyi to ask for his favorite concubine; though he did not dare refuse, in his heart he harbored resentment. Thereupon he exposed Shouwen's flight and desertion; Shouwen was executed in the market, and all considered it unjust.
translations.idiomatic: Shouwen came to ask for his favorite concubine. Congyi dared not refuse but nursed a grudge and exposed Shouwen's desertion. Shouwen was executed in the market, and everyone thought it unjust.

sentences.zh: 從義善擊毬，嘗侍太祖於便殿，命擊之。

translations.literal: Congyi was skilled at polo; he once attended Taizu in the informal hall and was ordered to play.
translations.idiomatic: Congyi was an expert polo player. Once in the informal hall Taizu ordered him to play.

sentences.zh: 從義易衣跨驢，馳驟殿庭，周旋擊拂，曲盡其妙。

translations.literal: Congyi changed clothes, mounted a donkey, galloped through the palace courtyard, and wheeled about striking and brushing the ball, fully displaying its subtle art.
translations.idiomatic: He changed clothes, mounted a donkey, and galloped through the courtyard, striking and parrying with perfect grace.

sentences.zh: 既罷，上賜坐，謂之曰：「卿技固精矣，然非將相所為。」

translations.literal: When it was over, the emperor granted him a seat and said: "Your skill is indeed refined, yet this is not what generals and ministers should do."
translations.idiomatic: When he finished, the emperor seated him and said, "Your skill is fine—but it is not what a minister should be doing."

sentences.zh: 從義大慚。

translations.literal: Congyi was greatly ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: Congyi was deeply ashamed.

sentences.zh: 子守忠、守信。

translations.literal: His sons were Shouzhong and Shouxin.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Shouzhong and Shouxin.

sentences.zh: 守忠至閑廄副使。

translations.literal: Shouzhong rose to deputy commissioner of the spare stables.
translations.idiomatic: Shouzhong rose to deputy commissioner of the spare stables.

sentences.zh: 守信字寶臣，頗知書，與士大夫遊，至東上閣門使、知邢州，卒。

translations.literal: Shouxin, style Baochen, was fairly learned in books and associated with scholar-officials; he rose to commissioner of the eastern upper gate and prefect of Xingzhou, then died.
translations.idiomatic: Shouxin, styled Baochen, was literate and moved among scholar-officials. He rose to eastern upper gate commissioner and prefect of Xingzhou, then died.

sentences.zh: 子世隆為比部員外郎。

translations.literal: His son Shilong was an outer-section director in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shilong served as outer-section director in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 世隆子昭祐、承祐。

translations.literal: Shilong's sons were Zhaoyou and Chengyou.
translations.idiomatic: Shilong's sons were Zhaoyou and Chengyou.

sentences.zh: 昭祐為閣門祗候。

translations.literal: Zhaoyou was a gate attendant of the privy chamber.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaoyou was a privy chamber gate attendant.

sentences.zh: 曾孫 承祐

translations.literal: Great-grandson Chengyou
translations.idiomatic: Great-grandson Chengyou

sentences.zh: 承祐，字天錫，娶舒王元偁女，授西頭供奉官。

translations.literal: Chengyou, style Tiansi, married a daughter of Prince Shu Yuan Cheng and was appointed western-head palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Chengyou, styled Tiansi, married a daughter of Prince Shu Yuan Cheng and was appointed western-head palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 仁宗為皇太子，承祐補左清道率府率、春坊左謁者，真宗為玉石小牌二，勒銘為戒飭之。

translations.literal: When Renzong was crown prince, Chengyou was appointed colonel of the Left Pure Path guard and left usher of the Eastern Palace; Zhenzong had two small jade and stone tablets made with inscriptions carved as admonitions to restrain him.
translations.idiomatic: When Renzong was crown prince, Chengyou became colonel of the Left Pure Path guard and left usher of the Eastern Palace. Zhenzong had two small jade tablets inscribed as warnings to keep him in line.

sentences.zh: 帝即位，遷西院副使兼閣道通事舍人、勾當翰林司，遷西上閣門副使。

translations.literal: When the emperor took the throne, Chengyou was transferred to deputy commissioner of the western court, concurrently privy-passage diplomatic usher and superintendent of the Hanlin office, then promoted to deputy commissioner of the western upper gate.
translations.idiomatic: When Renzong took the throne, Chengyou was made deputy commissioner of the western court, privy-passage usher, and superintendent of the Hanlin office, then deputy commissioner of the western upper gate.

sentences.zh: 坐盜御酒及用尚方金器除名，岳州編管，徙許州別駕。

translations.literal: For stealing imperial wine and using golden vessels from the imperial workshop he was struck from the rolls, placed under restricted residence at Yuezhou, and transferred to assistant administrator of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was dismissed for stealing imperial wine and using palace gold vessels, confined at Yuezhou, then sent to Xuzhou as assistant administrator.

sentences.zh: 起為率府率，遷西京作坊使、勾當右騏驥院。

translations.literal: He was recalled as colonel of the guard bureau, then transferred to commissioner of the western capital workshops and superintendent of the right fine-horse park.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as guard colonel, then made commissioner of the western capital workshops and superintendent of the right fine-horse park.

sentences.zh: 院之大校試路馬者，前鳴鞭擁御蓋，承祐代試之，其狂僭如此。

translations.literal: When the park's senior officer tested road horses, runners ahead cracked whips and bore the imperial parasol; Chengyou substituted himself in the test—such was his arrogance and presumption.
translations.idiomatic: When the park's senior officer tested road horses, runners cracked whips and bore the imperial parasol before him. Chengyou took the test himself—such was his arrogance.

sentences.zh: 進六宅使、象州團練使。

translations.literal: He was advanced to commissioner of the Six Residences and military commissioner of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to commissioner of the Six Residences and military commissioner of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 承祐性狡獪，緣東宮恩，又憑藉王邸親，既廢復用，廼僭言事，或指切人過失，同列謂之『武諫官』。

translations.literal: Chengyou was crafty and cunning by nature; relying on favor from the Eastern Palace and also on kinship with the prince's household, though once dismissed he was used again and then presumptuously spoke on affairs, sometimes pointing out others' faults—colleagues called him the "military remonstrance official."
translations.idiomatic: Chengyou was cunning. He traded on Eastern Palace favor and princely kinship, and after dismissal was brought back to speak out of turn on policy and pick at colleagues' faults. They nicknamed him the "military remonstrator."

sentences.zh: 真授衛州刺史、知相州，入為群牧副使，改濰州團練使，歷知曹、鄭、澶、鄆、貝州。

translations.literal: He was formally appointed prefect of Weizhou and acting prefect of Xiangzhou, entered service as deputy commissioner of the herds, was changed to military commissioner of Weifang, and successively acted as prefect of Cao, Zheng, Chan, Yun, and Bei.
translations.idiomatic: He was made prefect of Weizhou and acting prefect of Xiangzhou, then deputy herds commissioner, military commissioner of Weifang, and in turn prefect of Cao, Zheng, Chan, Yun, and Bei.

sentences.zh: 徙澶州兵馬總管，役卒有異謀者，廉得不待奏，捕斬之。

translations.literal: Transferred to overall commander of Chanzhou horse and foot, when corvée soldiers were found plotting sedition he did not wait to memorialize but captured and beheaded them.
translations.idiomatic: As overall commander at Chanzhou he learned that corvée troops were plotting rebellion, arrested them without waiting for court approval, and had them beheaded.

sentences.zh: 再知澶州，會中使過，遽延入問管軍闕補何人，使者曰：「聞朝廷方擇才武者。」

translations.literal: Again acting as prefect of Chanzhou, when a palace envoy passed through he hurriedly invited him in and asked who would fill the vacant military post; the envoy said: "I hear the court is selecting men of talent and martial skill."
translations.idiomatic: Serving again at Chanzhou, he detained a passing palace envoy and asked who would fill the vacant military post. The envoy said, "I hear the court is looking for a capable warrior."

sentences.zh: 承祐起挽彊自衒，左右皆笑。

translations.literal: Chengyou rose, drew the strong bow to show off, and those at his side all laughed.
translations.idiomatic: Chengyou stood, drew a strong bow to show off, and his attendants laughed.

sentences.zh: 入為龍神衛四廂都指揮使。

translations.literal: He entered service as overall commander of the four wings of the Dragon Spirit Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was made overall commander of the four wings of the Dragon Spirit Guard.

sentences.zh: 以父喪，起復真定府、定州等路副都總管。

translations.literal: On his father's death he was recalled from mourning to serve as deputy overall commander of the Zhending prefecture and Dingzhou circuit routes.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died he was recalled from mourning to serve as deputy overall commander on the Zhending and Dingzhou routes.

sentences.zh: 諫官歐陽脩、余靖論其非才，改知相州，尋徙大名府副都總管。

translations.literal: Remonstrance officials Ouyang Xiu and Yu Jing argued he lacked talent; he was changed to acting prefect of Xiangzhou, and soon transferred to deputy overall commander of Daming prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrators Ouyang Xiu and Yu Jing argued he was unfit. He was made acting prefect of Xiangzhou, then deputy overall commander at Daming.

sentences.zh: 樞密使杜衍惡承祐驕恣，奏罷軍權，為相州觀察使、永興軍副都總管，改知邢州，徙河陽兵馬總管。

translations.literal: Councilor-in-chief Du Yan hated Chengyou's arrogance and willfulness and memorialized to strip his military authority; he was made observation commissioner of Xiangzhou and deputy overall commander of Yongxing, then changed to acting prefect of Xingzhou and transferred to overall commander of Heyang horse and foot.
translations.idiomatic: Councilor Du Yan hated Chengyou's arrogance and stripped his military command, making him observation commissioner of Xiangzhou and deputy commander at Yongxing, then prefect of Xingzhou and overall commander at Heyang.

sentences.zh: 衍去位，復進為殿前都虞候、幷代州副都總管兼知代州，徙邢州。

translations.literal: When Yan left his post, Chengyou was again advanced to commandant of the palace front guard and deputy overall commander of Bing and Daizhou while concurrently acting prefect of Daizhou, then transferred to Xingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Du Yan left office, Chengyou was restored as commandant of the palace front guard and deputy overall commander of Bing and Daizhou while holding Daizhou, then transferred to Xingzhou.

sentences.zh: 諫官錢明逸言承祐無廉守，邢民素厭苦之，改相州，徙秦鳳路副總管。

translations.literal: Remonstrance official Qian Mingyi said Chengyou lacked integrity in office; the people of Xing had long been wearied and distressed by him. He was changed to Xiangzhou and transferred to deputy overall commander of the Qinfeng circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrator Qian Mingyi said Chengyou was corrupt and the people of Xing had long suffered under him. He was moved to Xiangzhou, then deputy overall commander on the Qinfeng circuit.

sentences.zh: 累遷建武軍節度使、殿前副都指揮使。

translations.literal: Through successive promotions he became military governor of Jianwu and deputy overall commander before the palace.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to military governor of Jianwu and deputy overall commander before the palace.

sentences.zh: 尋以宣徽南院使判應天府，府壁壘不完，盜至卒無以禦，承祐始城南關，浚沙、濉、盟三河。

translations.literal: Soon he was made southern commissioner of the Palace Secretariat acting for Yingtian prefecture. The prefectural walls and ramparts were incomplete; when bandits came the troops had nothing with which to resist. Chengyou first walled the southern pass, and dredged the Sha, Sui, and Meng rivers.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made southern Palace Secretariat commissioner for Yingtian. The walls were unfinished and bandits overran the city. Chengyou walled the southern gate and dredged the Sha, Sui, and Meng rivers.

sentences.zh: 徙亳州。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 諫官言承祐在應天府給糧不以次，且擅留糧綱，批宣頭，不發戍還兵，越法杖配輕罪，借用翰林器，出入擁旗槍，以禁兵同周衛，體涉狂僭，無人臣禮。

translations.literal: Remonstrance officials said that at Yingtian prefecture Chengyou distributed grain out of order, moreover detained grain convoys on his own authority, annotated imperial rescripts, did not release garrison troops returning from duty, exceeded the law in assigning light punishments by beating and exile, borrowed Hanlin equipment, went in and out escorted by banners and spears, and treated forbidden troops like Zhou royal guards—his conduct smacked of arrogance and presumption and lacked the rites of a subject.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrators charged that at Yingtian he issued grain out of turn, detained supply convoys, annotated imperial orders, held back returning garrison troops, punished minor offenses beyond his authority, borrowed Hanlin equipment, marched with banners and spears like a prince, and treated palace troops as a royal guard—conduct arrogant, presumptuous, and unbecoming a subject.

sentences.zh: 罷宣徽南院使，許州都總管，徙節保靜軍、知許州。

translations.literal: He was removed as southern commissioner of the Palace Secretariat, made overall commander of Xuzhou, and transferred to military governor of Baojing while acting prefect of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was stripped of his Palace Secretariat post, made overall commander of Xuzhou, and transferred to military governor of Baojing while holding Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 轉運使蘇舜元薦承祐有將帥才，政事如龔、黃。

translations.literal: Transport commissioner Su Shunyuan recommended Chengyou as having talent for generalship and administration like Gong and Huang.
translations.idiomatic: Transport commissioner Su Shunyuan recommended Chengyou as a general and administrator on par with Gong and Huang.

sentences.zh: 帝謂輔臣曰：「彼庸人，監司乃龔、黃比之，何所取信哉。」

translations.literal: The emperor said to chief ministers: "That mediocrity—and a supervisory official compares him to Gong and Huang; what is there to trust in that?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told his ministers, "That fool—and a supervisor compares him to Gong and Huang? Who could believe that?"

sentences.zh: 改知鄭州，未行，暴疾卒。

translations.literal: He was changed to acting prefect of Zhengzhou; before he could depart he died suddenly of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed acting prefect of Zhengzhou but died suddenly before he could take up the post.

sentences.zh: 贈太尉，謚曰密。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Grand Commandant with the posthumous title Mi.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Grand Commandant with the posthumous name Mi.

sentences.zh: 承祐所至，多興作為煩擾，百姓苦之。

translations.literal: Wherever Chengyou went he launched many construction projects that became a nuisance, and the common people suffered from them.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever Chengyou served he launched construction projects that harassed the people.

sentences.zh: 李洪信，幷州晉陽人，漢昭聖太后弟也。

translations.literal: Li Hongxin was a native of Jinyang in Bingzhou and younger brother of the Han empress dowager Zhaosheng.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hongxin came from Jinyang in Bingzhou and was the younger brother of Han empress dowager Zhaosheng.

sentences.zh: 后弟六人，洪信居長，少善騎射。

translations.literal: The empress had six younger brothers; Hongxin was the eldest. In youth he was skilled at mounted archery.
translations.idiomatic: The empress had six younger brothers, of whom Hongxin was the eldest. In youth he excelled at mounted archery.

sentences.zh: 後唐明宗在藩時，隸帳下，及即位，愛將朱弘實總領捧聖軍，弘實擢洪信為爪牙，漸遷小校。

translations.literal: When Later Tang's Emperor Mingzong was still in his princely establishment, Hongxin served under his banner; when Mingzong took the throne, his favored general Zhu Hongshi took overall command of the Fengsheng army and promoted Hongxin as his henchman, and he gradually rose to junior officer.
translations.idiomatic: When Later Tang's Emperor Mingzong was still a prince, Hongxin served in his retinue. After Mingzong acceded, his favored general Zhu Hongshi commanded the Fengsheng army and made Hongxin his henchman; Hongxin gradually rose to junior officer.

sentences.zh: 應順中，潞王舉兵，少帝弘實而東奔，捧聖軍數百騎從行，洪信預焉。

translations.literal: During Yingshun, the Prince of Lu raised troops; the young emperor and Hongshi fled east, and several hundred Fengsheng cavalry followed on the march, Hongxin among them.
translations.idiomatic: During Yingshun, the Prince of Lu rebelled. The young emperor fled east with Hongshi, followed by several hundred Fengsheng cavalry including Hongxin.

sentences.zh: 及次衛州，少帝與晉高祖遇，因有疑貳，謀害晉祖，其從兵皆亂。

translations.literal: When they reached Weizhou, the young emperor encountered the Jin founding emperor; because of mutual suspicion they plotted to kill the Jin ancestor, and his attendant troops all fell into disorder.
translations.idiomatic: At Weizhou the young emperor met the Jin founding emperor. Mutual suspicion led to a plot against him, and the attendant troops fell into chaos.

sentences.zh: 時漢祖方護晉祖，洪信以兵應之，獲免。

translations.literal: At that time the Han founding emperor was just protecting the Jin ancestor; Hongxin responded with troops and [the Jin ancestor] escaped harm.
translations.idiomatic: The Han founding emperor was then protecting the Jin emperor. Hongxin answered with troops, and the Jin emperor escaped harm.

sentences.zh: 清泰中，又為雍王重美牙校。

translations.literal: During Qingtai he again served as military adjutant to Prince Yong Chongmei.
translations.idiomatic: During Qingtai he again served as adjutant to Prince Yong Chongmei.

sentences.zh: 晉初，為興順左廂都指揮使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jin he was overall commander of the left wing of the Xingshun Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jin he was overall commander of the left wing of the Xingshun Guard.

sentences.zh: 漢祖統禁軍，遷鎮太原，奏隸麾下。

translations.literal: When the Han founding emperor took command of the palace army and was transferred to garrison Taiyuan, he memorialized to place Hongxin under his banner.
translations.idiomatic: When the Han emperor took command of the palace army and moved to Taiyuan, he brought Hongxin under his command.

sentences.zh: 漢祖領陳州刺史、左護聖左廂都指揮使，俄加岳州防禦使。

translations.literal: The Han founding emperor held the post of prefect of Chenzhou and overall commander of the left wing of the Left Sacred Guard; soon Hongxin was additionally made defender of Yuezhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Han emperor held Chenzhou and commanded the left wing of the Left Sacred Guard; soon Hongxin was also made defender of Yuezhou.

sentences.zh: 從漢祖降鄴，以警扈之勞，授侍衛馬軍都指揮使、領武信軍節度。

translations.literal: Following the Han founding emperor in surrendering Ye, for merit in escort and guard duty he was appointed overall commander of the palace guard cavalry and concurrent military governor of Wuxin.
translations.idiomatic: When the Han emperor took Ye, Hongxin was rewarded for escort duty with command of the palace cavalry and the Wuxin governorship.

sentences.zh: 乾祐中，以群小用事，心懷憂懼，白太后求解軍職，出為鎮寧軍節度。

translations.literal: During Ganyou, because petty men held power he was anxious in heart; he told the empress dowager he sought release from military office and was sent out as military governor of Zhenning.
translations.idiomatic: During Ganyou, with petty men in power, he grew fearful and asked the empress dowager to release him from military office. He was sent out as military governor of Zhenning.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，遷保義軍節度。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was transferred to military governor of Baoyi.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was transferred to military governor of Baoyi.

sentences.zh: 初，楊邠以元從功臣為方鎮者，不諳政務，令三司擇軍將分補諸鎮都押牙、孔目官，或恃以朝選，藩帥難制。

translations.literal: Earlier, Yang Bin, because founding followers who were regional commanders were unversed in administration, had the three fiscal offices select army officers to fill in as chief military adjutants and clerks in the various commands; some relied on court selection, and the military governors found them hard to control.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Yang Bin had noticed that founding followers serving as governors knew little of civil administration. He had fiscal offices assign army officers as adjutants and clerks in each command. Some relied on court backing, and governors could not control them.

sentences.zh: 洪信聞內難，即召馬步軍都校聶召，奉國軍校楊德、王建、黃全武、楊進、翟本，右牙都校任溫、武德，護聖都校康審澄及判官路濤、掌書記張洞、都押牙楊昭𠡽、孔目官魏守恭，悉殺之，誣奏謀逆。

translations.literal: Hongxin heard of internal turmoil and immediately summoned horse and foot army colonel Nie Zhao; Fengguo army officers Yang De, Wang Jian, Huang Quanwu, Yang Jin, and Zhai Ben; right-wing colonels Ren Wen and Wu De; Sacred Guard colonel Kang Shencheng; and administrative aide Lu Tao, chief secretary Zhang Dong, chief military adjutant Yang Zhao, and chief clerk Wei Shougong—and killed them all, falsely memorializing that they had plotted rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: When Hongxin heard of court turmoil he summoned colonel Nie Zhao, Fengguo officers Yang De, Wang Jian, Huang Quanwu, Yang Jin, and Zhai Ben, right-wing colonels Ren Wen and Wu De, Sacred Guard colonel Kang Shencheng, aide Lu Tao, secretary Zhang Dong, adjutant Yang Zhao, and clerk Wei Shougong—and killed them all, then falsely reported a plot against him.

sentences.zh: 周廣順初，加同平章事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhou Guangshun, [Hongxin] was given the additional title of co-equal chief councilor.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhou Guangshun, Hongxin was made co-equal chief councilor.

sentences.zh: 洪信常以此妄殺自歉，及革命，內不自安。

translations.literal: Hongxin often reproached himself for those wrongful killings; when the dynasty changed, he was inwardly ill at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Hongxin often reproached himself for those wrongful killings. When the dynasty changed, he grew inwardly uneasy.

sentences.zh: 周祖猶以漢太后之故，移鎮京兆。

translations.literal: The Zhou founder, still for the sake of the Han empress dowager, transferred him to garrison Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: For the Han empress dowager's sake, the Zhou founder transferred him to Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 本城兵不滿千，王峻西征至陜州，以援晉州為辭，又取去數百人。

translations.literal: The troops in his city numbered fewer than a thousand. When Wang Jun marched west and reached Shaanzhou, he took several hundred more on the pretext of reinforcing Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His city had fewer than a thousand troops. When Wang Jun marched west to Shaanzhou, he took several hundred more on the pretext of reinforcing Jinzhou.

sentences.zh: 及劉崇北遁，遣禁兵千餘屯京兆，洪信益懼，即請入朝，懇辭藩鎮，拜左武衛上將軍。

translations.literal: When Liu Chong fled north, more than a thousand palace troops were sent to garrison Jingzhao; Hongxin grew still more fearful, immediately asked to enter court, earnestly declined his regional command, and was appointed Grand General of the Left Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Chong fled north, more than a thousand palace troops garrisoned Jingzhao. Hongxin grew still more fearful, asked to come to court, declined his regional command, and was made Grand General of the Left Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 世宗即位，遷左驍衛上將軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong acceded, [Hongxin] was transferred to Grand General of the Left Valiant Guard.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong acceded, Hongxin was made Grand General of the Left Valiant Guard.

sentences.zh: 顯德五年，改右龍武軍統軍，從世宗北征，為合流口部署。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Xiande he was changed to overall commander of the Right Dragon Martial Guard; he followed Emperor Shizong on the northern campaign as commander at Heliukou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth Xiande year he became overall commander of the Right Dragon Martial Guard and followed Emperor Shizong on the northern campaign as commander at Heliukou.

sentences.zh: 乾德五年，改左驍衛上將軍。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Qiande he was changed to Grand General of the Left Valiant Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth Qiande year he was made Grand General of the Left Valiant Guard.

sentences.zh: 開寶五年請老，以本官致仕。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Kaibao he requested retirement and left office with his former title.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth Kaibao year he asked to retire and left office with his former rank.

sentences.zh: 八年，卒，年七十四。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he died, aged seventy-four.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the eighth year at seventy-four.

sentences.zh: 洪信無他才術，徒以外戚致位將相。

translations.literal: Hongxin had no other talent or skill; he reached the rank of general and minister solely through imperial affinal kinship.
translations.idiomatic: Hongxin had no real talent and reached general and minister solely through imperial kinship by marriage.

sentences.zh: 斂財累鉅萬，而吝嗇尤甚。

translations.literal: He amassed wealth totaling tens of thousands, yet was especially stingy and miserly.
translations.idiomatic: He amassed vast wealth yet was miserly in the extreme.

sentences.zh: 時節鎮皆廣置帳下親兵，惟洪信最寡少。

translations.literal: At that time all military governors widely maintained personal troops under their banners; only Hongxin had the fewest.
translations.idiomatic: Every governor maintained a large personal guard at the time—only Hongxin kept the smallest.

sentences.zh: 弟洪義。

translations.literal: His younger brother was Hongyi.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother was Hongyi.

sentences.zh: 弟 洪義

translations.literal: Younger brother Hongyi
translations.idiomatic: Younger brother Hongyi

sentences.zh: 洪義，本名洪威，避周祖名改焉。

translations.literal: Hongyi, original name Hongwei, changed it to avoid the Zhou founding ancestor's taboo name.
translations.idiomatic: Hongyi, originally named Hongwei, changed his name to avoid the Zhou founder's taboo.

sentences.zh: 漢祖鎮太原，補親校。

translations.literal: When the Han founding emperor garrisoned Taiyuan, Hongyi was appointed to his personal guard.
translations.idiomatic: When the Han emperor held Taiyuan, Hongyi joined his personal guard.

sentences.zh: 開國，授護聖左廂都校、領岳州防禦使，遷侍衛馬軍都指揮使、領武信軍節度。

translations.literal: At the founding of the state he was appointed colonel of the left wing of the Sacred Guard and concurrent defender of Yuezhou, then transferred to overall commander of the palace guard cavalry and concurrent military governor of Wuxin.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of Han he was made colonel of the left Sacred Guard wing and defender of Yuezhou, then commander of the palace cavalry and military governor of Wuxin.

sentences.zh: 少帝即位，改鎮寧軍節度。

translations.literal: When the young emperor acceded, [Hongyi] was changed to military governor of Zhenning.
translations.idiomatic: When the young emperor acceded, Hongyi was transferred to military governor of Zhenning.

sentences.zh: 會誅楊邠、史弘肇等，時侍衛步軍都指揮使王殷屯澶州，即遣供奉官孟業賫密詔令洪義殺之，又令護聖都指揮使郭崇等害周祖於鄴。

translations.literal: When Yang Bin, Shi Hongzhao, and others were executed, the overall commander of the palace guard infantry Wang Yin was then garrisoned at Chanzhou. [The court] immediately sent palace attendant Meng Ye bearing a secret edict ordering Hongyi to kill him, and also ordered the overall commander of the Sacred Guard Guo Chong and others to kill the Zhou founder at Ye.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Bin, Shi Hongzhao, and others were executed, palace infantry commander Wang Yin was garrisoned at Chanzhou. The court sent palace attendant Meng Ye with a secret edict ordering Hongyi to kill him, and also ordered Sacred Guard commander Guo Chong and others to kill the Zhou founder at Ye.

sentences.zh: 洪義素怯懦，慮殷覺，遷延不敢發，遽引業見殷，殷乃錮業，送密詔於周祖。

translations.literal: Hongyi had always been timid and cowardly; fearing Yin would notice, he delayed and dared not act, but abruptly brought Ye before Yin. Yin thereupon imprisoned Ye and sent the secret edict to the Zhou founder.
translations.idiomatic: Hongyi had always been timid. Fearing Yin would discover the plot, he delayed until he abruptly brought Ye to Yin. Yin imprisoned Ye and sent the secret edict to the Zhou founder.

sentences.zh: 洎周祖起兵，少帝又詔洪義扼河橋，及周祖兵至，洪義就降。

translations.literal: When the Zhou founder raised troops, the young emperor again ordered Hongyi to hold the river bridge; when the Zhou founder's army arrived, Hongyi submitted.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhou founder raised troops, the young emperor again ordered Hongyi to hold the river bridge. When the Zhou army arrived, Hongyi surrendered.

sentences.zh: 漢室之亡，由洪義也。

translations.literal: The fall of the Han house was due to Hongyi.
translations.idiomatic: The fall of the Han house was due to Hongyi.

sentences.zh: 廣順初，權知宋州節度，未幾，真拜歸德軍節度，加同平章事，權知許州，歲餘，改鎮安州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Guangshun he was acting military governor of Songzhou; before long he was formally appointed military governor of the Guide army, given the additional title of co-equal chief councilor, and made acting prefect of Xuzhou. After more than a year he was transferred to garrison Anzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Guangshun he acted as military governor of Songzhou. Soon he was formally made military governor of Guide, co-equal chief councilor, and acting prefect of Xuzhou. A year later he was transferred to Anzhou.

sentences.zh: 顯德初，加檢校太師。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiande he was given the additional title of Inspector Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xiande he was made Inspector Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 世宗即位，加兼侍中，未幾，徙青州。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong acceded, [Hongyi] was given the additional title of concurrent Palace Attendant; before long he was transferred to Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong acceded, Hongyi was made concurrent Palace Attendant and soon transferred to Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 六年夏，遷京兆尹、永興軍節度。

translations.literal: In the summer of the sixth year he was transferred to metropolitan prefect of Jingzhao and military governor of the Yongxing army.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the sixth year he became metropolitan prefect of Jingzhao and military governor of Yongxing.

sentences.zh: 恭帝嗣位，加開府階。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gongdi succeeded to the throne, [Hongyi] was given Ministerial rank.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gongdi succeeded to the throne, Hongyi was given Ministerial rank.

sentences.zh: 宋初，加兼中書令，移鄜州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song he was given the additional title of concurrent Chief Secretary and transferred to Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Song he was made concurrent Chief Secretary and transferred to Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 乾德五年，代歸。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Qiande he was replaced and returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth Qiande year he was recalled.

sentences.zh: 卒年五十九，贈太師。

translations.literal: He died aged fifty-nine and was posthumously made Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: He died at fifty-nine and was posthumously made Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 武行德

translations.literal: Wu Xingde
translations.idiomatic: Wu Xingde

sentences.zh: 武行德，幷州榆次人，身長九尺餘，材貌奇偉，家甚貧，常采樵鬻之自給。

translations.literal: Wu Xingde was a native of Yuci in Bingzhou; his body was more than nine chi tall, his build and appearance extraordinarily imposing. His family was very poor; he often gathered firewood and sold it to support himself.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Xingde came from Yuci in Bingzhou. He stood more than nine feet tall, with a striking presence. His family was poor, and he supported himself by gathering and selling firewood.

sentences.zh: 晉祖鎮幷門，暇日，從禽郊外，值行德負薪趨拱於道左，晉祖見其魁岸，又所負薪異常，令力士更舉之，俱不能舉，頗奇之，因留帳下。

translations.literal: When the Jin founding emperor garrisoned Bing Gate, on a leisure day he went hunting in the suburbs and encountered Xingde carrying firewood, hurrying to bow on the left of the road. The Jin founding emperor saw his towering stature and that the firewood he bore was unusual; he ordered strong men to try lifting it in turn, but none could lift it. He was quite struck by this and thereupon kept Xingde in his retinue.
translations.idiomatic: While garrisoning Bingzhou, the Jin emperor went hunting one day and saw Xingde on the road bowing with a load of firewood. His size and the unusual weight of the bundle struck the emperor, who had strong men try to lift it—none could. Impressed, he kept Xingde in his service.

sentences.zh: 晉天福初，授奉國都頭，遷指揮使，改控鶴指揮使、寧國軍都虞候。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jin Tianfu he was appointed head of the Fengguo Guard, promoted to commander, then changed to commander of the Crane Control Guard and commandant of the Ningguo army.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jin Tianfu reign he was made head of the Fengguo Guard, then commander, then commander of the Crane Control Guard and commandant of the Ningguo army.

sentences.zh: 開運中，契丹至汴，行德被獲，乃偽請於契丹以自效。

translations.literal: During Kaiyun the Khitan reached Bian; Xingde was captured and thereupon falsely asked the Khitan to serve them in order to save himself.
translations.idiomatic: During Kaiyun the Khitan took Bian and captured Xingde, who pretended to offer his service to them.

sentences.zh: 契丹信之，方具舟數十艘載鎧甲，令行德率將校軍卒送歸其國。

translations.literal: The Khitan trusted him; they were just preparing several dozen boats loaded with armor and ordered Xingde to lead officers and soldiers escorting them back to their country.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan trusted him and prepared dozens of boats loaded with armor for him to escort homeward with officers and troops.

sentences.zh: 溯汴至河陰，行德謂諸將曰：「我輩受國厚恩，而受制於契丹，與其離鄉井、投邊塞，為異域之鬼，曷若與諸君驅逐兇黨，共守河陽，姑俟契丹兵退，視天命所屬歸之，建功業，定禍亂，以圖富貴可乎？」
