translations.literal: Sailing up the Bian to Heyin, Xingde said to the generals: "We have received thick favor from the state yet are controlled by the Khitan. Rather than leave our home villages and throw ourselves on the frontier to become ghosts in a foreign land, how about joining you gentlemen in driving out the vicious band, holding Heyang together, waiting until Khitan troops withdraw, then seeing to whom Heaven's mandate belongs and submitting—establishing merit, settling turmoil, and seeking wealth and rank?"
translations.idiomatic: Sailing up the Bian to Heyin, Xingde told his officers, "We owe the state a great debt yet serve the Khitan. Better to drive out these invaders and hold Heyang together than die as exiles in a foreign land. When the Khitan withdraw, we can see where Heaven's mandate lies, win glory, end the chaos, and claim our reward—will you join me?"

sentences.zh: 眾素服行德威名，皆曰：「所向惟命，不敢愛死。」

translations.literal: The multitude had long respected Xingde's martial renown and all said: "We follow wherever you command and dare not spare our lives."
translations.idiomatic: The men had long respected Xingde's reputation. They answered, "We follow your command and will not spare our lives."

sentences.zh: 行德即殺契丹監使，分授器甲，由汜水倍道抵河陽。

translations.literal: Xingde immediately killed the Khitan supervising envoy, distributed weapons and armor, and by double marches through Sishui reached Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: Xingde killed the Khitan overseer, distributed arms and armor, and marched by forced pace through Sishui to Heyang.

sentences.zh: 契丹節度使崔廷勳出兵來拒，行德麾眾逆擊，自旦及午殊死戰，廷勳大敗，棄城走。

translations.literal: Khitan military governor Cui Tingxun led troops out to resist; Xingde commanded the multitude to strike back. From dawn until noon they fought a desperate battle; Tingxun was greatly defeated and abandoned the city in flight.
translations.idiomatic: Khitan governor Cui Tingxun marched out to resist. Xingde led a counterattack, and from dawn until noon they fought a desperate battle. Tingxun was routed and fled the city.

sentences.zh: 行德遂據河陽，盡以府庫分給將士，因推行德知州事。

translations.literal: Xingde thereupon held Heyang, distributed the entire treasury to officers and soldiers, and on that basis had Xingde act as prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Xingde seized Heyang, distributed the entire treasury to his troops, and took charge as acting prefect.

sentences.zh: 時契丹兵尚充斥，行德厲士卒，繕甲兵，據上遊，士氣益奮，人望歸之。

translations.literal: At that time Khitan troops still swarmed everywhere; Xingde roused the soldiers, repaired armor and weapons, and held the upper reaches of the river. Morale grew ever more ardent and men's hopes turned to him.
translations.idiomatic: Khitan troops still filled the region. Xingde hardened his men, repaired arms, and held the upper river. Morale soared and men looked to him as their leader.

sentences.zh: 聞漢祖起太原，即自稱河陽都部署，遣其弟行友間道奉表勸進，漢祖覽奏喜甚，即授行德河陽三城節度。

translations.literal: Hearing that the Han founding emperor had risen at Taiyuan, he immediately styled himself overall commander of Heyang, sent his younger brother Xingyou by a hidden route to present a memorial urging accession; the Han founding emperor read the memorial with great joy and immediately appointed Xingde military governor of the three Heyang cities.
translations.idiomatic: When he heard the Han emperor had risen at Taiyuan, he styled himself overall commander of Heyang and sent his brother Xingyou by a secret route with a memorial urging him to take the throne. The Han emperor was delighted and at once made Xingde military governor of the three Heyang cities.

sentences.zh: 漢祖由晉、絳至洛，行德迎候境上，以所部兵翼至京師，還河陽。

translations.literal: When the Han founding emperor went from Jin and Jiang to Luoyang, Xingde welcomed him at the border and with his own troops escorted him to the capital, then returned to Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: When the Han emperor marched from Jin and Jiang to Luoyang, Xingde met him at the border, escorted him to the capital with his troops, and returned to Heyang.

sentences.zh: 乾祐中，加同平章事，移真定尹、成德軍節度。

translations.literal: During Ganyou he was given the additional title of co-equal chief councilor and transferred to metropolitan magistrate of Zhending and military governor of Chengde.
translations.idiomatic: During Ganyou he was made co-equal chief councilor and transferred to metropolitan magistrate of Zhending and military governor of Chengde.

sentences.zh: 廣順初，加兼侍中，俄改忠武軍節度，遷河南尹、西京留守。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Guangshun he was given the additional title of Palace Attendant; soon he was changed to military governor of Zhongwu and transferred to metropolitan magistrate of Henan and western capital regent.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Guangshun he was made Palace Attendant, soon military governor of Zhongwu, then metropolitan magistrate of Henan and regent of the western capital.

sentences.zh: 時禁鹽入城，犯者法至死，告者給厚賞。

translations.literal: At that time bringing salt into the city was forbidden; violators were punished by death under law, and informers were given rich rewards.
translations.idiomatic: Salt was banned from the city on pain of death, with rich rewards for informers.

sentences.zh: 洛陽民家嫗將入城鬻蔬，俄有僧從嫗買蔬，就筥翻視，密置鹽筥中，少答其直，不買而去。

translations.literal: An old woman of a Luoyang household was about to enter the city to sell vegetables when suddenly a monk came from the woman to buy vegetables, leaned over the basket to look through it, secretly placed salt in the basket, paid her too little, and left without buying.
translations.idiomatic: An old woman was entering Luoyang to sell vegetables when a monk came to buy some, rummaged through her basket, secretly dropped salt into it, underpaid her, and left without buying.

sentences.zh: 嫗持入城，抱關者搜得鹽，擒以詣府。

translations.literal: The woman carried it into the city; the gate guards searched and found salt, seized her, and brought her to the prefectural office.
translations.idiomatic: She entered the city; gate guards found the salt, seized her, and brought her to the yamen.

sentences.zh: 行德見盛鹽襆非村嫗所有，疑而詰之，嫗言：「適有僧自城外買蔬，取視久之而去。」

translations.literal: Xingde saw that the bundle of salt was not something a village woman would own; suspecting this, he questioned her. The woman said: "Just now a monk from outside the city came to buy vegetables, looked through them for a long time, and left."
translations.idiomatic: Xingde saw that the salt bundle was not something a village woman would carry and questioned her. She said, "Just now a monk from outside the city came to buy vegetables, looked through them for a long time, and left."

sentences.zh: 即捕僧訊治之，具狀與關吏同誣以希賞。

translations.literal: He immediately arrested the monk and interrogated him; the full account showed he had acted together with the gate officials to frame her in hope of reward.
translations.idiomatic: He arrested the monk, who confessed that he and the gate guards had framed her for the reward.

sentences.zh: 行德釋嫗，斬僧及抱關吏數輩。

translations.literal: Xingde released the woman and beheaded the monk and several gate officials.
translations.idiomatic: Xingde released the woman and beheaded the monk and several gate guards.

sentences.zh: 人畏之若神明，部下凜然。

translations.literal: People feared him as if he were a spirit; subordinates were in awe.
translations.idiomatic: People feared him like a god, and his subordinates stood in awe.

sentences.zh: 三年，丁外艱，起復。

translations.literal: In the third year he mourned his father's death and was recalled from mourning to service.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, after his father's death, he was recalled from mourning to duty.

sentences.zh: 顯德初，加開府階，進封譙國公。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiande he was given Ministerial rank and advanced to Duke of Qiao.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xiande he received Ministerial rank and was advanced to Duke of Qiao.

sentences.zh: 世宗即位，兼中書令。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong acceded, [Xingde] was made concurrent Chief Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong acceded, Xingde was made concurrent Chief Secretary.

sentences.zh: 初，世宗處河東還，次河陽，以洛陽城頭缺，令葺之。

translations.literal: At first, when Emperor Shizong had settled Hedong and was returning, he halted at Heyang. Because the battlements of Luoyang were deficient, he ordered them repaired.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong had settled Hedong and was returning, he halted at Heyang. Finding Luoyang's battlements in disrepair, he ordered them restored.

sentences.zh: 行德率部民萬餘完其城，封邢國公。

translations.literal: Xingde led more than ten thousand local people to complete the city and was enfeoffed as Duke of Xing.
translations.idiomatic: Xingde led more than ten thousand local people to complete the walls and was enfeoffed as Duke of Xing.

sentences.zh: 是秋，代王晏為武寧軍節度，與晏兩換其任。

translations.literal: That autumn he replaced Wang Yan as military governor of the Wuning army, the two exchanging their posts.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn he and Wang Yan exchanged posts, Xingde taking the Wuning governorship.

sentences.zh: 先是，唐末楊氏據淮甸，自甬橋東南決汴，匯為汙澤。

translations.literal: Earlier, late in Tang the Yang clan held the Huai region; from Yongqiao southeast they breached the Bian River, which pooled into a foul marsh.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, late in Tang the Yang clan held the Huai region. Southeast of Yongqiao they breached the Bian River, turning it into a foul marsh.

sentences.zh: 二年，將議南征，遣行德率所部丁壯於古堤疏導之，東達於泗上。

translations.literal: In the second year, as a southern campaign was being planned, [the court] sent Xingde to lead the able-bodied men of his command in dredging and channeling it along the old embankment east as far as the Si River.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, as a southern campaign was planned, Xingde was sent to lead his able-bodied men in dredging the old embankment east to the Si River.

sentences.zh: 及親征，以行德為濠州行營都部署，破淮軍二千餘人於郡境。

translations.literal: When the emperor campaigned in person, Xingde was made overall commander of the Haozhou field headquarters and defeated more than two thousand Huai troops within the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On the personal campaign, Xingde was made overall commander at Haozhou and defeated more than two thousand Huai troops in the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 俄遣率師屯定遠以逼其城，為吳所敗，死者數百人，行德以身免，左授右衛上將軍。

translations.literal: Soon he was sent to lead troops garrisoned at Dingyuan to press the city; he was defeated by Wu, several hundred died, and Xingde escaped with his life. He was demoted and appointed Grand General of the Right Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he led troops to garrison Dingyuan and press the city, but Wu defeated him and several hundred died. Xingde escaped alive and was demoted to Grand General of the Right Guard.

sentences.zh: 五年，下淮南，復授行德保大軍節度兼中書令。

translations.literal: In the fifth year Huainan was taken; Xingde was again appointed military governor of the Baoda army and concurrent Chief Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, after Huainan fell, Xingde was again made military governor of Baoda and concurrent Chief Secretary.

sentences.zh: 恭帝嗣位，進封宋國公。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gongdi succeeded to the throne, [Xingde] was advanced and enfeoffed as Duke of Song.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gongdi succeeded to the throne, Xingde was advanced to Duke of Song.

sentences.zh: 宋初，加中書令，進封韓國公，再授忠武軍節度，改封魏國公。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song he was given Chief Secretary, advanced to Duke of Han, again appointed military governor of Zhongwu, and changed to Duke of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Song he was made Chief Secretary and Duke of Han, again military governor of Zhongwu, then advanced to Duke of Wei.

sentences.zh: 乾德二年，冬，移鎮安州，加開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qiande, in winter, he was transferred to garrison Anzhou and given the rank of opening a government office with ceremonial parity to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: In the second Qiande year, that winter, he was transferred to Anzhou and granted the privilege of an independent staff with ceremonial parity to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 開寶二年，入為太子太傅。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaibao he entered service as Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the second Kaibao year he was made Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 太平興國三年，以本官致仕。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taiping Xingguo he retired from office with his former title.
translations.idiomatic: In the third Taiping Xingguo year he retired with his former rank.

sentences.zh: 四年，卒，年七十二，贈太師。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he died, aged seventy-two, and was posthumously made Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourth year at seventy-two. The court posthumously made him Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 楊承信

translations.literal: Yang Chengxin
translations.idiomatic: Yang Chengxin

sentences.zh: 楊承信，字守真，其先沙陀部人。

translations.literal: Yang Chengxin, style Shouzhen, his ancestors were people of the Shatuo tribe.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Chengxin, styled Shouzhen, was descended from the Shatuo tribe.

sentences.zh: 父光遠，仕晉至太師、壽王。

translations.literal: His father Guangyuan served Jin to the rank of Grand Preceptor and Prince of Shou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Guangyuan served the Jin dynasty as Grand Preceptor and Prince of Shou.

sentences.zh: 承信，光遠第二子，幼以父任，自義武軍節院使領蘭州刺史，歷宣武、平盧二軍牙校。

translations.literal: Chengxin, Guangyuan's second son, in youth benefited from his father's position; from commissioner of the Yiwu army section he held the post of prefect of Lanzhou, and served as military adjutant in the Xuanwu and Pinglu armies.
translations.idiomatic: Chengxin was Guangyuan's second son. As a youth he rose on his father's coattails from Yiwu army commissioner to prefect of Lanzhou, and served as adjutant in the Xuanwu and Pinglu armies.

sentences.zh: 開運初，光遠以青州叛，少帝遣李守貞等討之，食盡勢窮，承信兄承勳劫其父以降，青州平，光遠死。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaiyun, Guangyuan rebelled from Qingzhou; the young emperor sent Li Shouzhen and others to attack him. When food was exhausted and their situation desperate, Chengxin's elder brother Chengxun seized their father to surrender. Qingzhou was pacified and Guangyuan died.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Kaiyun, Guangyuan rebelled from Qingzhou. The young emperor sent Li Shouzhen against him. When supplies ran out, Chengxin's brother Chengxun seized their father and surrendered. Qingzhou fell and Guangyuan was killed.

sentences.zh: 承信與弟承祚詣闕請死，詔釋之，以承信為右羽林將軍，承祚為右驍衛將軍，放歸，服喪私第，尋安置鄭州。

translations.literal: Chengxin and his younger brother Chengzuo went to court to request death; an edict pardoned them. Chengxin was made general of the Right Forest of Feathers Guard, Chengzuo general of the Right Valiant Guard; they were released, mourned at a private residence, and soon were settled at Zhengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chengxin and his brother Chengzuo went to court to beg for death. The emperor pardoned them, made Chengxin a general of the Right Forest of Feathers Guard and Chengzuo a general of the Right Valiant Guard, and sent them home to mourn. Soon they were resettled at Zhengzhou.

sentences.zh: 初，光遠送款契丹求援，兵未至而光遠降。

translations.literal: Earlier, Guangyuan had sent allegiance to the Khitan seeking aid; the troops had not yet arrived when Guangyuan surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Guangyuan had appealed to the Khitan for help, but surrendered before their troops arrived.

sentences.zh: 及契丹來寇，承勳時為鄭州防禦使，召數其罪殺之。

translations.literal: When the Khitan came to raid, Chengxun was then defender of Zhengzhou; he summoned the Khitan envoy, enumerated his crimes, and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan invaded, Chengxun was defender of Zhengzhou. He summoned their envoy, listed his crimes, and executed him.

sentences.zh: 以承信為平戶軍節度，繼父職。

translations.literal: Chengxin was made military governor of the Pinghu army and succeeded to his father's post.
translations.idiomatic: Chengxin was made military governor of Pinglu, succeeding his father's post.

sentences.zh: 仕漢歷安、鄜二州節度，累加檢校太師。

translations.literal: Serving Han, he successively held the military governorships of An and Fu prefectures and was repeatedly given the additional title of Inspector Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: Under Han he governed An and Fu in turn and was repeatedly made Inspector Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 周廣順初，加同平章事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhou Guangshun, [Chengxin] was given the additional title of co-equal chief councilor.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhou Guangshun, Chengxin was made co-equal chief councilor.

sentences.zh: 諸將西討劉崇，承信表求預行。

translations.literal: As the generals marched west to attack Liu Chong, Chengxin memorialized asking to take part in the campaign.
translations.idiomatic: When the generals marched west against Liu Chong, Chengxin asked to join the campaign.

sentences.zh: 以郊祀恩加開府階，封杞國公。

translations.literal: By grace of the suburban sacrifice he was given Ministerial rank and enfeoffed as Duke of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: By grace of the suburban sacrifice he received Ministerial rank and was enfeoffed as Duke of Qi.

sentences.zh: 世宗即位，進韓國公。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong acceded, [Chengxin] was advanced to Duke of Han.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong acceded, Chengxin was advanced to Duke of Han.

sentences.zh: 顯德初，征淮南，為濠州攻城副都部署，改壽州北砦都部署兼知行府事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiande, on the Huainan campaign, he served as deputy overall commander for the siege of Haozhou, then was changed to overall commander of the northern stockade at Shouzhou, concurrently administering prefectural affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xiande, during the Huainan campaign, he served as deputy siege commander at Haozhou, then became commander of the northern stockade at Shouzhou while administering prefectural affairs.

sentences.zh: 壽州平，累戰功，擢忠正軍節度、同平章事。

translations.literal: When Shouzhou was pacified, for repeated battle merit he was promoted to military governor of the Zhongzheng army and co-equal chief councilor.
translations.idiomatic: After Shouzhou fell, repeated battle merit won him the Zhongzheng governorship and the title of co-equal chief councilor.

sentences.zh: 時徙州治下蔡，承信既增廣其城，又遣監軍薛友柔敗淮人六百餘於廬州北。

translations.literal: At that time the prefectural seat was moved to Xiaocai; Chengxin both enlarged the city and sent supervisory commissioner Xue Yourou to defeat more than six hundred Huai men north of Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the prefectural seat moved to Xiaocai, Chengxin enlarged the city and sent supervisory commissioner Xue Yourou to defeat more than six hundred Huai troops north of Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 恭帝即位，進封魯國公。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gongdi acceded, [Chengxin] was advanced and enfeoffed as Duke of Lu.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gongdi acceded, Chengxin was advanced to Duke of Lu.

sentences.zh: 宋初，加兼侍中，來朝，會征李筠，命為澤州西面都部署，筠平，移鎮河中。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song he was given the additional title of concurrent Palace Attendant and came to court. When Li Jun was attacked, he was appointed overall western commander at Zezhou; after Jun was pacified, he was transferred to garrison Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Song he was made concurrent Palace Attendant and came to court. During the campaign against Li Jun he was made western commander at Zezhou, and after Jun fell he was transferred to Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 乾德元年，進封趙國公。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qiande he was advanced and enfeoffed as Duke of Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: In the first Qiande year he was advanced to Duke of Zhao.

sentences.zh: 二年，卒，年四十四，贈中書令。

translations.literal: In the second year he died, aged forty-four, and was posthumously made Chief Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second year at forty-four and was posthumously made Chief Secretary.

sentences.zh: 承信身長八尺，美儀表，善持論，且多藝能，雖叛臣之子，然累歷藩鎮，刻勵為政而不苛，故能始終富貴。

translations.literal: Chengxin was eight chi tall, with handsome bearing, skilled at discourse, and possessed of many talents. Though the son of a rebel minister, he repeatedly held regional commands, strove in administration without harshness, and therefore could remain wealthy and honored from beginning to end.
translations.idiomatic: Chengxin stood eight feet tall, with a fine presence, a ready tongue, and many talents. Though a rebel's son, he held one command after another, governed diligently without cruelty, and kept wealth and rank to the end.

sentences.zh: 其卒也，蒲民表乞祠之，則其遺愛之在人者，可知矣。

translations.literal: When he died, the people of Pu submitted a petition asking to sacrifice to him; thus how his lingering kindness toward men may be known.
translations.idiomatic: When he died the people of Pu petitioned for a shrine in his honor—proof enough of the affection he left behind.

sentences.zh: 景德四年，錄其孫松為奉職。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jingde, his grandson Song was recorded and appointed to a palace attendant post.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth Jingde year his grandson Song was appointed to a palace attendant post.

sentences.zh: 侯章，幷州榆次人。

translations.literal: Hou Zhang was a native of Yuci in Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Zhang came from Yuci in Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 初在幷門事後唐莊宗為隊長，明宗朝遷小校。

translations.literal: At first at Bing Gate he served Later Tang's Emperor Zhuangzong as squad leader; in Mingzong's reign he was promoted to junior officer.
translations.idiomatic: He first served Emperor Zhuangzong at Bingzhou as a squad leader and rose to junior officer under Mingzong.

sentences.zh: 晉開運末，為忠衛指揮使，屯兵陜州，為內外馬步軍都指揮使兼三城巡檢使。

translations.literal: At the end of Jin Kaiyun he was commander of the Loyal Guard, garrisoned troops at Shaanzhou, and served as overall commander of the inner and outer horse and foot armies, concurrently patrol commissioner of the three cities.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Jin Kaiyun reign he commanded the Loyal Guard at Shaanzhou and served as overall commander of the inner and outer armies and patrol commissioner of the three cities.

sentences.zh: 會契丹入中原，與趙暉、王晏謀斬契丹將劉愿，送款於漢祖。

translations.literal: When the Khitan entered the central plains, together with Zhao Hui and Wang Yan he plotted to behead the Khitan general Liu Yuan and sent allegiance to the Han founding emperor.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan overran the central plains, he joined Zhao Hui and Wang Yan in killing the Khitan general Liu Yuan and submitting to the Han emperor.

sentences.zh: 漢祖入汴，擢為鎮國軍節度。

translations.literal: When the Han founding emperor entered Bian, Zhang was promoted to military governor of Zhenguo.
translations.idiomatic: When the Han emperor entered Bian, Zhang was made military governor of Zhenguo.

sentences.zh: 乾祐初，加同平章事，尋移鎮邠州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Ganyou he was given the additional title of co-equal chief councilor; soon he was transferred to garrison Binzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Ganyou he was made co-equal chief councilor and soon transferred to Binzhou.

sentences.zh: 章居鎮無善政，傲上剝下，以貪猥聞，用見戶為逃，擅其租賦，乃矯奏貧民數千戶負稅租，久禁繫不能輸，願以己俸代。

translations.literal: While holding his command Zhang had no good administration; he was arrogant toward superiors and exploited subordinates, and was known for greed and baseness. He treated registered households as fugitives and seized their rents and taxes, then falsely memorialized that several thousand poor households owed tax and rent, had long been imprisoned unable to pay, and asked to substitute his own salary.
translations.idiomatic: In his command Zhang governed badly—arrogant to superiors, harsh on subordinates, notorious for greed. He treated taxpayers as fugitives, seized their dues, then falsely reported that thousands of poor households owed back taxes, had been imprisoned unable to pay, and offered to cover the debt from his own salary.

sentences.zh: 時方姑息，詔褒之。

translations.literal: The times were ones of indulgence and forbearance; an edict praised him.
translations.idiomatic: The court was in an indulgent mood and issued an edict praising him.

sentences.zh: 副使趙彥鐸有良馬，章欲之不與，誣彥鐸謀逆之，殺之，亦置而不問。

translations.literal: Deputy commissioner Zhao Yanduo had a fine horse; Zhang wanted it but Yanduo would not give it. Zhang falsely accused Yanduo of plotting rebellion and killed him; this too was set aside without inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: Deputy Zhao Yanduo owned a fine horse. Zhang demanded it, was refused, falsely accused Zhao of treason, and killed him—with no consequences.

sentences.zh: 俄加檢校太師。

translations.literal: Soon he was given the additional title of Inspector Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made Inspector Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 周初，加兼侍中。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhou, [Zhang] was given the additional title of concurrent Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhou, Zhang was made concurrent Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 廣順二年入朝，獻銀帛，請開宴，周祖謂左右曰：「諸侯來朝，天子自當錫宴，以申愷樂，豈俟其貢奉為之耶？」

translations.literal: In the second year of Guangshun he entered court, presented silver and silks, and asked that a banquet be opened. The Zhou founder said to those beside him: "When feudal lords come to court, the Son of Heaven ought himself to grant a banquet to express cordial joy—how could one wait for their tribute and offerings to do it?"
translations.idiomatic: In the second Guangshun year he came to court with silver and silks and asked for a banquet. The Zhou founder told his attendants, "When feudal lords come to court, the Son of Heaven should grant a feast himself to show cordial joy—why wait for their tribute?"

sentences.zh: 使復賜之。

translations.literal: He had [the gifts] returned and bestowed again.
translations.idiomatic: He had the gifts returned and bestowed again.

sentences.zh: 仍令有司自今藩鎮有進奉者勿受。

translations.literal: He also ordered the relevant offices that from then on they were not to accept offerings presented by regional commands.
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered the relevant offices never again to accept tribute offerings from regional commands.

sentences.zh: 俄賜宴廣政殿，章又獻銀千兩、馬七匹上壽，復不納。

translations.literal: Soon a banquet was granted in Guangzheng Hall; Zhang again presented a thousand taels of silver and seven horses as birthday offerings, and again they were not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Soon a banquet was granted in Guangzheng Hall. Zhang again offered a thousand taels of silver and seven horses as birthday gifts, and again they were refused.

sentences.zh: 三年，授鄧州節度。

translations.literal: In the third year he was appointed military governor of Dengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was made military governor of Dengzhou.

sentences.zh: 周祖親郊，加開府階，封申國公。

translations.literal: When the Zhou founder performed the suburban sacrifice in person, [Zhang] was given Ministerial rank and enfeoffed as Duke of Shen.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhou founder performed the suburban sacrifice in person, Zhang received Ministerial rank and was enfeoffed as Duke of Shen.

sentences.zh: 世宗即位，加兼中書令。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong acceded, [Zhang] was given the additional title of concurrent Chief Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong acceded, Zhang was made concurrent Chief Secretary.

sentences.zh: 世宗親征壽陽，命章為攻城水砦都部署，右衛大將軍王璨副之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong personally campaigned against Shouyang, he appointed Zhang overall commander of the siege water stockades, with Grand General of the Right Guard Wang Can as his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong personally campaigned against Shouyang, he made Zhang overall commander of the siege water stockades, with Right Guard Grand General Wang Can as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 俄徙西北水砦都部署，再為武勝軍節度。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to overall commander of the northwestern water stockades, and again served as military governor of the Wusheng army.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was transferred to command the northwestern water stockades and again made military governor of Wusheng.

sentences.zh: 建隆元年八月，授太子太師，封楚國公。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the first year of Jianlong he was appointed Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent and enfeoffed as Duke of Chu.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the first Jianlong year he was appointed Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent and enfeoffed as Duke of Chu.

sentences.zh: 既罷節鎮，居常怏怏。

translations.literal: Once removed from his military command, he was habitually discontented.
translations.idiomatic: After losing his military command, he was habitually discontented.

sentences.zh: 一日於朝堂與故舊言晉、漢間事，時有輕忽章者，章厲聲曰：「當遼主疾作謀歸，有上書請避暑嵩山者，我麤人，以戰鬥取富貴，若此諛佞，未嘗為之！」

translations.literal: One day in the court hall he spoke with old associates of affairs between Jin and Han; at the time some slighted Zhang, and Zhang said in a stern voice: "When the Liao ruler fell ill and plotted to return home, someone memorialized asking to escape the heat on Mount Song—I am a rough man who won wealth and rank through battle; such flattery and sycophancy I have never practiced!"
translations.idiomatic: One day in the court hall he spoke with old associates of Jin and Han times. When some slighted him, Zhang said sharply, "When the Liao ruler fell ill and plotted to return home, someone memorialized asking to escape the heat on Mount Song—I am a rough soldier who won fortune in battle. I have never practiced such flattery!"

sentences.zh: 坐中有慚者。

translations.literal: Among those seated there were some who felt ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: Some of those present were ashamed.

sentences.zh: 乾德五年，卒。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Qiande he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fifth Qiande year.

sentences.zh: 論曰：王景輩微時，或至為盜、負薪，遭五代之亂，奮身戎功，重據邊要。

translations.literal: The commentary says: Men like Wang Jing, in humble times, sometimes became bandits or carried firewood; encountering the chaos of the Five Dynasties, they threw themselves into military merit and heavily held frontier posts of importance.
translations.idiomatic: The commentators observe: Men like Wang Jing, in their youth, were sometimes bandits or woodcutters. In the chaos of the Five Dynasties they threw themselves into military service and came to hold weighty frontier commands.

sentences.zh: 宋興，稽顙北嚮，太祖待以誠信，宜無不自安者。

translations.literal: When Song arose, they bowed their foreheads and turned north; Taizu treated them with sincerity and trust, and they ought all to have felt secure.
translations.idiomatic: When the Song rose, they kowtowed to the north and Taizu treated them with sincerity. They should have had nothing to fear.

sentences.zh: 景趨利改圖，乃至滅族。

translations.literal: Jing, pursuing profit, changed his course, even to the extermination of his clan.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Jing, chasing profit, changed course—and brought his clan to ruin.

sentences.zh: 王晏、郭從義遷怒肆忿，誣人以死。

translations.literal: Wang Yan and Guo Congyi shifted anger and vented wrath, framing men to death.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yan and Guo Congyi vented their rage on others and framed innocent men to death.

sentences.zh: 侯章在藩邸有剝下之名，李洪義狃於肺腑之戚，而無外凜之志，咎孰甚焉！

translations.literal: Hou Zhang had a reputation at his regional command for stripping subordinates; Li Hongyi was accustomed to kinship of flesh and blood yet lacked outward awe-inspiring resolve—whose fault was the greater!
translations.idiomatic: Hou Zhang was known for exploiting his subjects. Li Hongyi rested on family ties and lacked the outward sternness a commander needs—who was more to blame?

sentences.zh: 斯皆亂世之習，有不能盡去之者。

translations.literal: These were all habits of a chaotic age; there were some that could not be entirely cast off.
translations.idiomatic: All of this was the habit of a chaotic age—habits not easily shed.

sentences.zh: 武行德守洛邑，辯究欺罔，民用畏服，顧不優於諸人耶？

translations.literal: Wu Xingde held Luoyang, investigated and exposed deception, and the people in consequence feared and submitted—was he not rather superior to the others?
translations.idiomatic: Wu Xingde held Luoyang, exposed fraud, and made the people fear and obey—was he not the better of them all?
